V      Profit distribution plan or plan for the capitalization of capital reserve during the Reporting Period resolved by the board

       During the Reporting Period, the Company realized a net profit attributable to shareholders of the Company of approximately
       RMB4,593,871,000, and earnings per share of approximately RMB0.9119. The board of directors of the Company proposed to
       distribute cash dividends of RMB0.49 per share (tax inclusive) to all shareholders based on the total share capital of 5,037,747,500
       shares. The proposed dividends are expected to be paid on 13 July 2026.

       The total distribution amount is fixed. Should there be a change in the issued shares of the Company prior to the record date, the
       dividend per share may be adjusted and an announcement will be made accordingly.

             Explanation for retrospective adjustments or restatements:

             Pursuant to the resolution passed at the 2021 annual general meeting, the Company acquired a 100% equity interest in YS
             Energy Company for a consideration of RMB2,457,000,000. As both the Company and YS Energy Company were under the
             control of Jiangsu Communications Holding Co., Ltd. before and after the Company’s acquisition of 100% equity interest in
             YS Energy Company, and such control was not temporary, the Company consolidated YS Energy Company in accordance
             with the China Accounting Standards and made corresponding retrospective adjustments to the comparative figures in the
             previous period.

             Meanwhile, the Group implemented the “Interpretation No. 15 of Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises” (Cai
             Kuai [2021] No. 35) issued by the Ministry of Finance during 2022, which became effective from 1 January 2022. The
             Company made retrospective adjustments in accordance with this interpretation for trial-run sales that occurred between 1
             January 2021 and the date of initial application.

                  Description of the Company’s principal accounting data and financial indicators for the previous three years at the end of
                  the Reporting Period

                   ✓   Applicable                          Not applicable

                  During the Reporting Period, the Company achieved operating revenue of approximately RMB20.289 billion, representing
                  a year-on-year decrease of approximately 12.54% and an increase of approximately 33.55% compared to 2023. Excluding
                  the impact of construction revenue, the Company recorded operating revenue of approximately RMB12.134 billion,
                  representing a year-on-year decrease of approximately 1.61% and a decrease of approximately 4.43% compared to 2023.
                  This was primarily attributable to a decline in revenue from petroleum product sales and real estate business, influenced
                  by factors such as fluctuations in crude oil prices and the scale of real estate project deliveries. During the Reporting
                  Period, the Company recorded toll revenue of approximately RMB9.555 billion, representing a year-on-year increase of
                  approximately 0.29% and an increase of approximately 0.47% compared to 2023.

                  During the Reporting Period, the Company’s gross operating margin (excluding construction revenue and costs) increased
                  by 0.84 percentage points year-on-year and by 6.09 percentage points compared with the end of 2023. This was affected
                  by factors such as the change in the dividend cycle of Bank of Jiangsu (dividends recognised in 2025 were RMB168 million;
                  dividends recognised in 2024 were approximately RMB608 million; dividends recognised in 2023 were approximately
                  RMB384 million; and the average dividends recognised in the past three years were approximately RMB386 million), the
                  total profit for the Reporting Period decreased by approximately 3.34% year-on-year but increased by approximately 7.64%
                  compared with the end of 2023. After excluding the impact of dividends from Bank of Jiangsu, the net profit attributable
                  to shareholders of the listed company of the Company was approximately RMB4.426 billion, representing a year-on-year
                  increase of approximately 2.00% and an increase of approximately 9.85% compared with 2023.

                  During the Reporting Period, benefiting from the growth in toll revenue and various cost reduction and efficiency
                  enhancement measures implemented by the Company, overall costs and expenses decreased year-on-year. The gross
                  operating profit for the Reporting Period increased compared to the same period last year. Net cash flow from operating
                  activities increased by approximately 7.05% compared to the same period last year but decreased by approximately 8.53%
                  compared to the end of 2023, primarily due to increased tax payments compared to 2023 and a reduction in factoring
                  business following the transfer of equity in the factoring company.

14   Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited

I   BUSINESS OF THE COMPANY DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
    (I)   Company status

          The Company was incorporated in Jiangsu Province of the People’s Republic of China on 1 August 1992 and is the only
          listed road and bridge investment and operation company in Jiangsu Province. On 27 June 1997, 1,222 million H shares
          issued by the Company were listed on the HKEX. On 16 January 2001, 150 million A shares issued by the Company were
          listed on the SSE. On 23 December 2002, the Group established a Level 1 American Depositary Receipt (ADR) program for
          trading in the US over-the-counter market. As at the end of the Reporting Period, the Company had a total share capital of
          5,037,747,500 shares with a par value of RMB1 per share.

          The Company is principally engaged in the investment, construction, operation and management of toll roads and bridges
          in Jiangsu Province and the development of service areas along expressways. In addition to the Jiangsu section of the
          Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway, the Company has full or partial interests in toll roads and bridges in Jiangsu Province,
          including the Ningchang Expressway, Zhenli Expressway, Guangjing Expressway, Xicheng Expressway, Xiyi Expressway,
          Zhendan Expressway, Changyi Expressway, Yichang Expressway and Wufengshan Toll Bridge, Ningyang Yangtze River
          Bridge, Yanjiang Expressway, Jiangyin Bridge, Sujiahang Expressway and Changjia Expressway. As at the end of the
          Reporting Period, the Company controlled 12 road and bridge projects currently in operation, and 3 newly constructed road
          and bridge projects, and invested directly into 4 other road and bridge projects, with a total length of approximately 1,000
          kilometres.

          The Company’s operating areas are located in the Yangtze River Delta, which is the most economically vibrant region in
          the PRC. The road and bridge projects owned or invested by the Company involve the roads and bridges serving as the
          major transport corridors linking roads stretching east-to-west and south-to-north across the Jiangsu Province. The Jiangsu
          Section of Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway, being the Company’s core assets, links six large and medium cities namely
          Shanghai, Suzhou, Wuxi, Changzhou, Zhenjiang and Nanjing, and is one of the busiest expressways in the PRC.

          In addition, the Company is also actively exploring and developing its transportation+, and clean energy business, in order
          to further expand its profitability and achieve sustainable development for the Company. As at the end of the Reporting
          Period, the Company directly owns seven wholly-owned subsidiaries, six non wholly-owned subsidiaries and nine associates
          and joint ventures, indirectly owned eight wholly-owned subsidiaries, nine non wholly-owned subsidiaries and eight associates
          and joint ventures, with total assets of approximately RMB96.389 billion and net assets attributable to shareholders of the
          listed company amounting to RMB41.443 billion.

          Subsidiaries directly controlled or invested by the Company are as follows:

           (II)   Business of the Company During the Reporting Period

                  As of the end of 2025, the Company reported total assets of approximately RMB96.389 billion, and the net assets
                  attributable to shareholders of the listed company were approximately RMB41.443 billion. During the Reporting Period, the
                  Company achieved annual revenue of approximately RMB20.289 billion, representing a year-on-year decrease of about
                  12.54%. Excluding the impact of construction revenue, the Company achieved revenue of approximately RMB12.134 billion,
                  a year-on-year decrease of about 1.61%. Affected by factors such as the change in the dividend cycle of Bank of Jiangsu,
                  the Company recorded total profit of approximately RMB6.106 billion, a year-on-year decrease of approximately 3.34%;
                  net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company was approximately RMB4.594 billion, a year-on-year decrease
                  of approximately 7.13%; basic earnings per share was RMB0.9119; net operating cash flow was approximately RMB6.762
                  billion; and weighted average return on net assets was 11.48%.

                  According to the “Notice on Matters Related to Vehicle Rescue Service Charges” jointly issued by the Jiangsu Provincial
                  Development and Reform Commission and the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Transportation, the towing and crane fees
                  for vehicle rescue services on Jiangsu’s expressways shall be exempted from 1 September 2025. The rescue vehicles shall
                  be the responsibility of the operating entities of each expressway. To accurately reflect the actual situation of the Company’s
                  market-oriented business, effective from the end of the Reporting Period, the “Obstacle Clearance Business” originally under
                  “Ancillary Services” has been adjusted to an independent business segment.

to facilitate investors’ reading and understanding, starting from the end of this Reporting Period, non-service area leasing
businesses originally under “Ancillary Services” have been consolidated into “Other Businesses”; leasing businesses
related to property companies originally under “Other Businesses” have been consolidated into “Property Business”.

The aforementioned adjustments only involve the presentation format of business information and do not affect the
Company’s consolidated financial statements, including revenue, operating costs, and total profit. The comparative figures
for the previous year have been retrospectively adjusted in this report.

47.10% of the Group’s total operating revenue, and accounted for approximately 78.75% after excluding construction
revenue. Among them, the average daily toll revenue of Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway was approximately RMB15,082,000,
a year-on-year increase of approximately 4.93%.

Note 1:   Affected by the expansion works of the Shanghai-Wuhan Expressway (Taicang to Changzhou section) commencing in November
          2024, traffic along the Yanjiang Expressway was restricted. During the Reporting Period, toll revenue from the Ningchang Expressway,
          which connects to the Yanjiang Expressway, decreased year-on-year, while the toll revenue of the Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway
          (parallel to the Yanjiang Expressway) increased year-on-year.

Note 2:   Affected by the full closure for expansion works of the Zhenjiang South to Dantu Junction section of the Yangli Expressway (under
          the Company’s management) commencing in April 2025, the toll revenue of the Zhenli Expressway for the current Reporting Period
          decreased year-on-year; due to the impact of these works, the toll revenue of the Wufengshan Bridge for the current Reporting Period
          increased year-on-year. As of the end of the Reporting Period, this construction project had been completed and opened to traffic
          ahead of the planned schedule.

Note 3:   Affected by the half-closure construction for expansion of the section from Xueyan Hub to Xiwu Hub on the Huyi Expressway in March
          2024, the toll revenue of the Xiyi Expressway and the Changyi Expressway decreased year-on-year during the Reporting Period.
          As of the end of the Reporting Period, the construction project has been completed and opened to traffic according to the planned
          schedule.

Note 4:   Affected by the full closure for expansion works of the Guangling Junction to Jingjiang Junction section of the Beijing-Shanghai
          Expressway commencing in June 2025, the toll revenue of the Guangjing Expressway and the Xicheng Expressway for the current
          Reporting Period decreased year-on-year.

Note 5:   During the Reporting Period, the number of days with toll exemptions for small passenger vehicles during major holidays was 24 days,
          and the actual number of toll collection days in the current year was 341 days, representing a decrease of 1 day compared with the
          previous year.


Ancillary services business. During the Reporting Period, the Group’s ancillary services business achieved revenue of
approximately RMB1,629,182,000, representing a decrease of approximately 4.57% year-on-year. Specifically, oil product
sales generated revenue of approximately RMB1,446,027,000, a decrease of approximately 4.89% year-on-year. The total
sales volume of oil products during this Reporting Period increased by 2.74% year-on-year, but the gross profit margin for
oil product sales decreased by 2.07% year-on-year due to the narrowing of the spread between purchase and sale prices.
The Company’s self-operated charging piles commenced operation progressively from April 2025, generating revenue of
approximately RMB11,724,000 from the charging business. Revenue from other businesses, such as service area leasing,
amounted to approximately RMB171,431,000, a decrease of approximately 8.21% year-on-year, primarily due to reduced
service area leasing income resulting from the expansion of the northern section of the Guangjing Expressway and the
renovation of the Gehu and Meicun service areas.

Clean energy business. During the Reporting Period, affected by factors such as fluctuations in wind resources and
industry regulation, Rudong offshore wind power project of YS Energy Company recorded a decrease of on-grid electricity
consumption, and the Group’s electricity sales revenue reached approximately RMB685,134,000, a year-on-year decrease
of approximately 4.81%.

Property business. The Group’s property business is primarily operated by its subsidiaries, Ninghu Properties Company
and Hanwei Company. During the Reporting Period, the Group’s property business revenue was approximately75,074,000,
representing a year-on-year decrease of approximately 55.64%, mainly due to the smaller scale of property projects
delivered compared to the same period of the previous year.

Obstacle clearance business. During the Reporting Period, the Group’s towing and obstacle clearance business
generated revenue of approximately RMB6,444,000, representing a year-on-year decrease of approximately 34.14%. This

     II    INDUSTRY OF THE COMPANY DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
           (I)     Basic Situation of the Road Transportation Industry

                   2025 saw the national economy maintained its stable and positive trajectory, with high-quality development advancing
                   further. As a “bellwether” of economic activity, the performance of the transportation industry is highly correlated with
                   GDP growth and total social output value. China’s GDP in 2025 exceeded RMB140 trillion, representing a year-on-year
                   increase of 5%. The steady release of domestic demand and the deeper integration of regional economies provided a solid
                   foundation for road transportation.

                   Supported by a robust macroeconomic environment, the supply side of expressways has gradually entered the phase of
                   “enhancing quality of existing assets”. At present, the national expressway network, particularly the backbone national
                   corridors, has achieved a high degree of connectivity. Against the backdrop of tightening land resources in core economic
                   zones and increasing environmental protection requirements, the scarcity of high-quality road assets in key regions has
                   been further consolidated.

                   As the layout of the road network aligns more closely with travel demand, the traffic structure of the industry has
                   demonstrated considerable resilience. Currently, passenger vehicle traffic dominates the road network, with a blend of
                   short-distance trips and long-distance self-driving demand forming a stable foundation for toll revenue. In terms of freight
                   transport, precision logistics, primarily involving high-value-added and time-sensitive goods, has become the norm for
                   operations along core corridors. Furthermore, “digital and intelligent empowerment” and “green and low-carbon
                   initiatives” are emerging as new engines driving the industry’s high-quality transformation and development.

           (II)    Position of the Company in the industry

                   In terms of geographical location, the Company is the only listed road and bridge investment and operation company in
                   Jiangsu Province, focusing on the continuous integration of high-quality road and bridge projects in the road network of
                   southern Jiangsu. The roads operated by the Group occupy a dominant position in the expressway network of southern
                   Jiangsu. Jiangsu Province is one of China’s most economically developed provinces, characterised by strong vitality
                   in its non-public sector economy. In 2025, Jiangsu’s regional GDP exceeded RMB14 trillion, representing a year-on-
                   year increase of 5.3%. The increment maintained its position as the highest in the nation. The economic aggregate has
                   consecutively crossed the thresholds of RMB4 trillion over the past five years. As the most economically developed region
                   in Jiangsu Province, the southern Jiangsu area supports sustained growth in traffic demand through its robust industrial
                   synergy and active trade environment.

                   In terms of market image, the Shanghai Stock Exchange has awarded the Company the highest rating of A for its
                   information disclosure assessment for six consecutive years. In 2025, the Company received multiple prestigious awards,
                   including the “China Listed Companies Investor Relations Shareholder Return Pegasus Award” from Securities Times,
                   the “China Listed Companies Yinghua A-Share Value Demonstration Case” from China Fund News, and the “2025
                   Annual Shareholder Return Golden Bull Award” from China Securities Journal. Additionally, it was honored with the “China
                   Listed Companies Yinghua H-Share Value Demonstration Case” in the Hong Kong stock market. These accolades reflect
                   recognition from various capital markets for the Company’s intrinsic value and its commitment to standardised operations.

                   In terms of operating results, the Company’s performance indicators ranked top among listed companies in the same
                   industry. Although the reconstruction and expansion projects have posed certain challenges to operational efficiency and toll
                   revenue in the short term, upon completion, these projects will extend the toll collection period and enhance service quality,
                   reserving broad space and benefits for the Company’s sustainable development. Moreover, the Company has always
                   maintained a high dividends payout ratio since its listing with continuous dividend distributions underscoring its commitment
                   as a listed enterprise to ensure long-term and stable returns for shareholders.

           (III)   Policies relating to road transportation industry

                   The Regulations for the Administration of Toll Highways (《收 費 公 路 管 理 條 例》), which came into effect on 1 November
                   2004, has been organised for amendment since 2013 and has been open for public consultation twice in 2013 and 2015.
                   On 20 December 2018, the Ministry of Transport issued the draft amendments on the Regulations for the Administration of
                   Toll Highways. Currently, the time of official promulgation of the revised Regulations for the Administration of Toll Highways
                   has not yet been determined. On 11 May 2024, the General Office of the State Council issued the “2024 Legislative
                   Work Plan of the State Council”, which listed the “Regulations for the Administration of Toll Highways” as one of the
                   administrative regulations to be formulated or revised in 2024. On 12 May 2025, the Ministry of Transport included the
                   “Regulations on the Administration of Toll Highways (Revision)” in its annual legislative work plan as a “legislative project
                   to be completed within the ministry or published within the year”. Currently, the time of official promulgation of the revised
                   Regulations for the Administration of Toll Highways has not yet been determined.

On 15 February 2020, the Ministry of Transport issued a notice that from 00:00 midnight on 17 February 2020 until the end
of the containment measures, toll roads payment nationwide would be waived; on 28 April 2020, the Ministry of Transport
issued a notice that the toll roads payment legally approved by the law would be resumed from 00:00 midnight on 6
May 2020. The Ministry of Transport, the National Development and Reform Commission and other eight ministries and
commissions issued a notice, which clearly required the provincial governments and relevant operating entities to extend
the payment period of toll roads through negotiation, signing of contracts and other means in accordance with relevant
regulations, and compensate certain amount during the toll-free period accordingly. Till now, Jiangsu Province has not
specified the toll-free compensation policy for expressways under the Group’s management.

On 2 June 2021, the Ministry of Transport and other three departments issued the Implementation Plan for Comprehensively
Promoting Differentiated Toll Collection on Expressways (《全 面 推 廣 高 速 公 路 差 異 化 收 費 實 施 方 案》), proposing to
comprehensively promote differentiated toll on expressways. From 00:00 on 1 July 2024 to 24:00 on 30 June 2025, Nanjing
City, Jiangsu Province, implemented a pilot program for differentiated toll policies on expressways in Lishui District and
Gaochun District. The Dongping Toll Station of G4221 Shanghai-Wuhan Expressway managed by the Group is included
in the preferential scope. Vehicles being in compliance with the preferential condition can be charged half of the toll fees,
and the toll fees for vehicles that conduct the differentiated preferential policy are paid to the Group by the Transportation
Bureau of Lishui District, Nanjing City. In June 2025, the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Transportation issued a letter
agreeing to the extension of the differentiated toll policy for certain expressways in Lishui District and Gaochun District of
Nanjing Municipality for three years (from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2028) in accordance with existing policies. In addition, the
Taihu Tunnel of the Changzhou-Wuxi section of the Suzhou-Wuxi-Changzhou Southern Expressway, which is managed by
the Group under an entrusted management arrangement, implements a differentiated toll policy. The Wuxi Municipal Bureau
of Transportation, through a service purchase agreement, provides toll concessions for non-commercial ETC-equipped
passenger vehicles registered in Wuxi with a certified seating capacity of nine persons or fewer. In December 2024, the
Jiangsu Provincial Department of Transportation issued a letter agreeing to the continuation of the differentiated toll policy
for the Taihu Tunnel for three years (from 30 December 2024 to 29 December 2027). The eligible vehicles and concessionary
route remain unchanged, while the preferential toll rate is adjusted from RMB15 per trip to RMB10 per trip.

On 16 January 2023, the Jiangsu Provincial People’s Government issued General Policy Measures on Promoting the First
Overall Improvement in Economic Operation (《關 於 推 動 經 濟 運 行 率 先 整 體 好 轉 若 干 政 策 措 施》), giving a 15% discount
on ETC tolls for expressway passenger buses with 30 or more passes per month (inclusive) and a 15% discount on tolls
for freight vehicles with the Yunzheng Sutong Card. A 50% discount on ETC tolls at all general road toll stations and
expressways in the province will be given for international standard container transport vehicles entering and exiting major
container ports in the province with an annual throughput of over 2 million TEUs or an annual throughput of 1 million TEUs
and a growth rate exceeding the average growth level of the province for three consecutive years (currently the eligible ports
are Taicang Port, Lianyungang Port, Nanjing Port and Nantong Port), with the implementation period from 1 April 2023 to
31 December 2027. For container transport vehicles entering and leaving the main loading points and collection points for
containers of the China-Europe (Asia) Express in the province, full exemption of vehicle tolls will continue at all ordinary road
toll stations and expressways in the province until 31 December 2027.

On 25 July 2024, the Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Finance officially announced the list in relation to the first
batch of demonstration areas for the digital transformation and upgrade regarding road and waterway transportation
infrastructure, and Jiangsu Province was as one of the first batch selected among eight demonstration regions. The Jiangsu
section of the Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway, Ningchang Expressway and Zhenli Expressway managed by the Group are all
within the scope of the demonstration area, and investments in eligible digital transformation construction can be subsidized
up to 40%.

On 8 May 2025, the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Transportation, the Jiangsu Provincial Development and Reform
Commission, and the Jiangsu Provincial Department of Finance jointly issued the “Notice on Optimising and Improving
Preferential Toll Policies for Certain Trucks in Our Province” (《關於優化完善我省部分貨車車輛通行費優惠政策的通知》). It
specifies that from 16 May 2025, on sections of the road network operating at Level 2 service level or below, a differentiated
toll discount of 15% will be implemented for Class 3–6 trucks equipped with and normally using ETC for payment. For the
Taihu Tunnel on the Southern Suzhou-Wuxi-Changzhou Expressway and the Nanjing-Yangzhou Yangtze River Bridge,
where tolls are charged per passage, the road section operating entities may, based on the approved toll standard as the
upper limit and considering the operational and traffic flow conditions of the sections, independently decide to implement
a differentiated toll discount of no less than 15% for all trucks equipped with and normally using ETC for payment. The
specific discount rate will be announced to the public by the road section operating entities. The policy implementation
period is 2 years. Concurrently, the previous preferential policy of offering a ETC-equipped trucks holding the “Yunzheng
Sutong Card” a 15% discount on toll charges has been discontinued. The Group’s Zhenjiang-Danyang Expressway and
the Huantaihu Expressway offer a ETC-equipped and properly used 3–6-class trucks a 15% discount on tolls. The Nanjing-
Yangzhou Yangtze River Bridge offers a ETC-equipped and properly used trucks a 15% discount. The Taihu Tunnel, part of
the Changzhou Qianhuang Hub-Wuxi Nanquan Hub managed under the Group’s trusteeship, offers a ETC-equipped and
properly used trucks a 30% discount on tolls.

     III   DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF THE OPERATIONS
           In 2025, the Company, based on consolidating its core advantages in the road and bridge business, driven by deepening digital
           and intelligent integration and innovation, following the path of accelerating green and low-carbon transformation, and with the goal
           of cultivating sustainable growth momentum, promoted deep synergy across various business segments, entering a new stage
           characterised by enhanced capability and superior quality and efficiency.

           1.      Road and bridge operations

                   Consolidating the foundation of core business, the Company made steady progress in the construction of major
                   projects. Firstly, the Ningyang Yangtze River Bridge North Connection Project has been successfully opened
                   to traffic. The total estimated investment of the project is approximately RMB6.985 billion, with the Company investing
                   RMB2.095 billion as capital, accounting for 60.00% of the project capital. During the Reporting Period, construction
                   investment amounted to approximately RMB942 million, with a cumulative construction investment of approximately
                   RMB5.045 billion, representing 72.23% of the total project investment. On 1 January 2026, the Ningyang Yangtze River
                   Bridge North Connection Project officially commenced operations. Secondly, the Wuxi-Yixing Expressway Xueyan
                   Hub-Xiwu Hub section expansion project was successfully completed. The project has a total estimated investment
                   of approximately RMB7.75491 billion, with the Company’s non wholly owned subsidiary, Guangjing Xicheng Company,
                   contributing approximately RMB3.10196 billion in the entire capital. During the Reporting Period, construction investment
                   amounted to approximately RMB3.676 million, with a cumulative construction investment of approximately RMB5.823
                   billion, representing 75.09% of the total project investment. On 11 December 2025, the southern section of the Wuxi–Yixing
                   Expressway commenced operations. Thirdly, Xitai Project was initiated. The total estimated investment of the project
                   is approximately RMB24.198 billion, with the Company investing RMB5.747 billion as capital, accounting for 47.50% of the
                   project capital. During the Reporting Period, construction investment amounted to approximately RMB1.445 billion, with a
                   cumulative construction investment of approximately RMB7.511 billion, representing 31.04% of the total project investment.
                   The project commenced in November 2024 and is expected to be completed and open to traffic in 2028. Fourthly, the
                   Danyang-Jintan Project was orderly progressed. The total estimated investment of the project is approximately
                   RMB14.563 billion, with the Company investing RMB3.908 billion as capital, accounting for 74.60% of the project capital.
                   During the Reporting Period, construction investment amounted to approximately RMB1.585 billion, with a cumulative
                   construction investment of approximately RMB3.289 billion, representing 22.58% of the total project investment. The project
                   commenced in November 2024 and is expected to be completed and open to traffic by the end of 2028. Fifthly, the
                   Company invested in the Expansion Project of Guangjing North Section. The project has a total estimated investment
                   of approximately RMB2.905 billion, with the Company’s non wholly owned subsidiary, Guangjing Xicheng Company,
                   contributing approximately RMB1.452 billion in the entire capital. During the Reporting Period, construction investment
                   amounted to approximately RMB422 million, with a cumulative construction investment of approximately RMB745 billion,
                   representing 25.65% of the total project investment. The project’s pilot section commenced construction in September
                   2024 and is expected to open to traffic by the end of 2028. Sixth, the Company conducted forward-looking research
                   on the planning for the expansion of the Jiangsu section of the Shanghai-Nanjing (Huning) Expressway. During
                   the Reporting Period, the Company steadily advanced the optimization study on the expansion plan for the Shanghai-
                   Nanjing Expressway, conducted on-site research in multiple locations, and has substantially completed the investigation and
                   analysis of restrictive factors for the expansion.

Focusing on intelligent operations, multiple measures are implemented to enhance the efficiency of the road
network. The Company leveraged digital and intelligent transformation as a key driver to comprehensively optimise the
operational performance of the road network. Firstly, the self-service transformation of toll lanes was deepened to
break through traffic bottlenecks at stations. During the Reporting Period, 118 additional toll robots were deployed,
raising the self-service ratio of mixed lanes to approximately 95%. Building on the pilot of station-level intelligent systems
at Nanjing Toll Station, simultaneous increases in peak vehicle throughput and response speed were achieved. Secondly,
the Company optimised intelligent capacity expansion solutions to achieve precise management control and
decision-making. During the Reporting Period, intelligent capacity expansion upgrades were completed on approximately
130 kilometres of key road sections. The algorithms for perception, prediction, and decision-making were upgraded from
being experience-driven to data-driven, increasing the effectiveness of control strategies to approximately 92%. The
“Research and Demonstration Application of Complete Technology for Smart Capacity Expansion on Jiangsu Expressways”,
in which the Company participated in the application, was awarded the Special Prize of the 2025 China Highway and
Transportation Society Science and Technology Award. The related technology was selected as a typical experience for the
pilot programme of building China into a country with a strong transport network by the Ministry of Transport. Thirdly, the
Company has improved the joint service support system to reduce the duration of special situation handling.
Deepening the “One Road, Three Parties” joint service mechanism, and leveraging 33 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) airports
to establish a three-dimensional rescue network, further enhancing the proactive detection and safety warning capabilities
for various special situations, and creating a “5-minute rescue zone”. During the Reporting Period, a total of 49,800
emergency rescue tasks were handled. The average response time and average handling time for clearance and rescue
operations improved by approximately 26.47% and 27.41% year-on-year, respectively. This resulted in approximately
38.90% reduction in congestion points during holidays and approximately 12.10% decrease in the accident rate per million
vehicle-kilometres. Fourth, the Company has innovated travel services and deeply explored the potential of the
road network to attract traffic and increase revenue. During the Reporting Period, the Company actively carried out
the “Operation Revitalisation” initiative, adding multi-functional service counters at toll stations and service areas, achieving
a service response rate of 100%. For logistics and oversized cargo transport customer groups”, one-to-one” customised
solutions were implemented, successfully guiding 15,000 vehicle trips for precise network entry. This not only optimised user
experience but also drove an increase in toll revenue for the road network exceeding RMB10 million.

Adhering to lean maintenance and guided by technology, the Company improved the level of road and bridge
maintenance. The Company adhered to the principle of optimising the total life-cycle cost, promoting the improvement
of quality and efficiency in maintenance management. First, core technical indicators has been maintained at high
levels to consolidate the quality foundation of road assets. During the Reporting Period, the MQI1 and PQI2 for all
Company’s road sections remained consistently above 95. The proportion of Class 1 and Class 23 bridges was maintained
at 100%, tunnel assessment results were all Class 1, and highway technical condition indicators continued to improve.
Second, the Company has implemented the “near-zero impact” maintenance model to reduce interference from
lane-occupying works. Through intensive maintenance and coordinated air-ground patrols, the frequency and duration of
lane-occupying works were significantly reduced by 18.85% and 25.06% year-on-year, respectively, minimising the impact
of maintenance construction on public travel. Third, the Company has tackled fundamental safety improvements to
enhance the overall safety level of the entire network. The Company continued to advance the construction of the
Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway safety excellence project, achieving an overall reduction of approximately 57% for the number
of fatal accidents at accident-prone sections. It was selected as the only representative from the province to be included
in the national list of “Excellence Projects for the Refined Enhancement of Highway Safety Facilities and Traffic Order
Management”.

1
        MQI: Maintenance Quality Indicator, an indicator used to describe the technical condition of a specific highway section and the
        required maintenance level. An MQI value of 90–100 is considered excellent, indicating that the pavement is in good condition and
        does not require major repairs or renovations.
2
        PQI: Pavement Quality Index, an indicator used to assess the quality of road surfaces, typically employed to evaluate the surface
        condition of highways. The PQI value is calculated based on factors such as the smoothness of the road surface, longitudinal and
        transverse slopes, cracks, and damage. A PQI value of 90–100 is considered excellent.
3
        According to the Standards for Technical Condition Evaluation of Highway Bridges《公路橋樑技術狀況評定標準》) (JTGT H21-2011),
        the overall technical conditions of bridges are divided into five classes: Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, Class 4 and Class 5. Among them,
        Class 1 indicates the bridge is new and fully functional, while Class 2 shows minor defects that do not affect its function.

           Outstanding financing platforms. The Group maintains the listing status on two exchanges (in Hong Kong and Shanghai) and is
           traded in three cities (Hong Kong, Shanghai and New York) and achieves sound operation and sustainable performance growth with
           high credit rating, low gearing ratio and strong solvency. The Group achieved outstanding results in investor relations management
           and owns a stable investors base and an excellent market image in domestic and overseas capital markets thanks to its long-term
           policies with high proportion of cash dividend. The Group will continue to improve its financing structure and reduce financing costs
           in the future development through leveraging on the capital market’s efficient financing channels.

Explanation of reasons for changes in operating income: This was primarily due to a year-on-year decrease in
construction investment in road and bridge projects during the Reporting Period and the corresponding decrease in
construction period costs.

Explanation of reasons for changes in operating costs: This was mainly due to the year-on-year decrease in
construction investment in road and bridge projects during the Reporting Period and the corresponding decrease in
construction period costs.

Explanation of reasons for changes in sales expenses: This was primarily due to a year-on-year decrease in
expenses such as employee costs during the Reporting Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in administrative expenses: This was primarily attributable to a year-on-year
reduction in expenses amortisation costs related to renovation and expansion projects during the Reporting Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in financial expenses: This was mainly due to the decrease in the domestic loan
market quotation rate (LPR) and the Company’s proactive and effective financing measures during the Reporting
Period, which led to a year-on-year decrease in the consolidated borrowing rate of interest-bearing debt charged to
interest, and a corresponding decrease in finance costs.

Explanation of reasons for changes in R&D expenses: This was mainly attributable to the amortisation expenses for
the digital platform project invested in by YS Energy Company during the Reporting Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in net cash flow from operating activities:During the Reporting Period, the
Company’s toll revenue increased year-on-year, while various costs and expenses decreased year-on-year due to
effective measures implemented to reduce costs and enhance efficiency, resulting in a year-on-year decrease in net
cash flow from operating activities.

Explanation of reasons for changes in net cash flow generated from investing activities: This was mainly due to the
year-on-year decrease in construction investment in road and bridge projects during the Reporting Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in net cash flow generated from financing activities: This was primarily due to
the Company’s proactive optimisation of its capital structure and control over debt scale, resulting in a year-on-year
decrease in net cash inflow from borrowings and capital contributions received by subsidiaries during the Reporting
Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in fair value gains: This was mainly attributable to a narrower fair value loss on
other non-current financial assets held by subsidiaries during the Reporting Period compared with the same period
last year.

Explanation of reasons for changes in investment income: This was primarily attributable to a significant reduction in
dividends from Bank of Jiangsu Co., Ltd. due to an adjustment in its dividend distribution cycle during the Reporting
Period, as well as a year-on-year decrease in investment income contributed by associated enterprises.

Explanation of the reasons for the change in asset disposal income: This was primarily due to the recognition of a
gain on disposal of assets arising from the termination of toll collection on the Luma First Class Highway last year.

Explanation of reasons for changes in credit impairment losses: This was mainly due to the recovery of receivables
in the previous year and the provision for bad debts based on the balance of receivables during the Reporting
Period.

Explanation of changes in other income: This was primarily attributable to the recognition of government subsidies
for the Xiyi Expressway expansion and upgrading project during the Reporting Period.

Explanation of reasons for changes in other income: This was primarily attributable to a decrease in the fair value
changes of other equity instrument investments held by the Group during the Reporting Period compared with the
same period last year.

                  3.     Expenses

                          ✓    Applicable                     Not Applicable

                         (1)     Administrative expenses

                                  During the Reporting Period, the Group’s cumulative administrative expenses incurred were approximately
                                  RMB282,051,000, representing a decrease of approximately 5.54% compared with the same period last
                                  year. This was primarily attributable to a year-on-year reduction in expenses such as amortisation costs
                                  related to renovation and expansion projects during the Reporting Period.

                         (2)     Financial expenses

                                  During the Reporting Period, financial expenses incurred by the Group were approximately
                                  RMB832,187,000 in aggregate, representing a decrease by approximately 13.01% over the same period
                                  of the previous year. The decrease in financial expenses was mainly due to the corresponding decrease in
                                  financial expenses as a result of the year-on-year decrease in interest-bearing debt consolidated borrowing
                                  rate of the Company’s interest expenses with the Company’s proactive and effective financing measures
                                  such as optimizing the overall debt structure of the Group and grasping the financing window in the market.

                         (3)     Selling expenses

                                  During the Reporting Period, the Group’s aggregate selling expenses were approximately RMB5,747,000,
                                  representing a year-on-year decrease of approximately 3.31% compared to the same period last year. This
                                  was mainly due to the year-on-year decrease in expenses such as employee costs during the Reporting
                                  Period.

                         (4)     Taxes and surcharges

                                  During the Reporting Period, the taxes and surcharges incurred by the Group were RMB88,660,000 in
                                  aggregate, representing a year-on-year decrease of approximately 25.77%. This was primarily attributable
                                  to a year-on-year decrease in land appreciation tax incurred by the Company during the Reporting Period.

                         (5)     Income tax

                                  The statutory income tax rate for companies of the Group was 25%, 16.5% etc. During the Reporting
                                  Period, the income tax expense of the Group was approximately RMB1,284,153,000, representing a
                                  year-on-year increase of approximately 12.01%. This was mainly due to the year-on-year increase in the
                                  Group’s taxable income for the Reporting Period.

               measures, which led to a decrease in various costs and expenses compared to the same period last year, all of
               which contributed to the increase in the net cash flow from operating activities compared with the same period
               last year. The net cash outflow from investment activities was approximately RMB5,321,894,000, representing
               a decrease of approximately 43.31% year-on-year, mainly due to the year-on-year decrease in construction
               investment of road and bridge projects during the Reporting Period. The net cash outflow from financing activities
               was approximately RMB1,678,066,000, compared to a net inflow of approximately RMB3,081,233,000 in the same
               period last year. This was primarily due to the Company’s proactive optimisation of its capital structure and control
               of debt scale. During the Reporting Period, the net cash inflow from borrowings obtained by the Company and the
               capital contributions received by subsidiaries, resulting in a year-on-year increase in the net cash flow from financing
               activities.

     (2)     Capital structure and solvency

              The Group focuses on maintaining a reasonable capital structure and continuously improving profitability
              to maintain the Group’s good credit rating and sound financial condition. The total liabilities at the end of
              the Reporting Period were approximately RMB41,408,029,000, and the Group’s total asset-liability ratio
              was approximately 42.96%, a decrease of approximately 1.71% as compared with the end of the previous
              period. Based on the Group’s stable and abundant operating cash flow and good financing and capital
              management capabilities, the management believes that the financial leverage ratio at the end of the
              Reporting Period remained at a safe level.

                         (3)   Financial strategy and financing arrangement

                                During the Reporting Period, the Group actively expanded its financing channels, adjusted its debt structure
                                and reduced financing costs. By embracing a proactive financing strategy, the Company successfully
                                fulfilled its funding requirements for its operations, management and project investment while managing
                                its financing costs effectively. The Group’s borrowing requirements are not subject to seasonality. During
                                the Reporting Period, an additional fund of approximately RMB11,536,960,000 was obtained through
                                direct financing. As at 31 December 2025, the Group’s borrowings amounted to RMB24,381,300,980, of
                                which RMB5,823,776,430 were fixed-rate loans. As at the end of the Reporting Period, the balance of the
                                principal of interest-bearing liabilities was approximately RMB32,543,025,260, representing a decrease of
                                approximately RMB862,649,890 compared to the beginning of the period, of which short-term interest-
                                bearing liabilities accounted for approximately 13.21% and long-term interest-bearing liabilities accounted
                                for approximately 86.79%. The Group’s consolidated borrowing cost for interest-bearing liabilities was
                                approximately 2.26%, a decrease of approximately 0.52% compared to the end of 2024, and approximately
                                1.07% lower than the current Loan Prime Rate (LPR).

                         (4)   Credit policy

                                In order to minimize credit risk, the Group has controlled credit limits, undertaken credit approvals and
                                implemented other control procedures to ensure that necessary follow-up actions are taken to recover
                                overdue debts. In addition, the Group reviews the recovery of its receivables on each balance sheet date
                                to ensure that adequate provisions are made for credit impairment. In view of the above, the management
                                considers that the Group’s credit risk is relatively low.

                         (5)   Contingencies

                                As an industrial practice in the real estate industry, Ninghu Properties Company, a subsidiary of the
                                Company, provides joint and several guarantees in connection with mortgage loans granted to buyers of
                                commodity housing properties. The guarantee obligation shall begin from the effective date of a guarantee
                                contract and cease when the registration of mortgage in respect of a purchased property is completed and
                                the Building Right Encumbrances Certificate is delivered to and received by banks. As at 31 December
                                2025, the outstanding guarantees amounted to approximately RMB108,252,485.28 (31 December 2024:
                                RMB138,169,867.02).

VI.   DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF THE COMPANY ON ITS FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

      (I)    Industry landscape and development trends
             ✓    Applicable                  Not Applicable

             From the supply-side perspective, the expressway sector currently exhibits a dual-track trend of “network densification
             and refinement” alongside “capacity expansion and quality enhancement”. The ongoing advancement of the national
             highway network layout plan has set a long-term direction for the construction of a high-quality, comprehensive, and multi-
             dimensional transportation network. From the perspective of industry practice, the main arterial corridors in core regions
             such as the Yangtze River Delta have entered a peak period of reconstruction and expansion. In response to the growing
             traffic pressure, the expansion and upgrading of existing road assets have not only significantly enhanced the overall traffic
             capacity and service level of the road network but also effectively extended the concession period of high-quality assets,
             laying the foundation for the sustainable operation of the industry. Furthermore, with the deep integration of digitalisation-
             driven smart transportation initiatives into road asset operations, the operational efficiency and management precision of the
             road network will be further elevated.

             From the demand-side perspective, transportation demand demonstrates strong certainty. In terms of passenger transport,
             benefiting from the continuous growth in private car ownership and the normalisation of cross-regional travel and tourism,
             passenger vehicle traffic has maintained steady growth, exhibiting distinct regional and holiday concentration characteristics.
             Regarding freight transport, as the domestic industrial structure advances towards mid-to-high-end levels, the requirements
             for transit timeliness from high-value-added manufacturing, express logistics, and cold chain transportation have significantly
             increased, driving the transformation of freight demand towards professional and efficiency. Particularly with the deepening
             implementation of the Yangtze River Delta integration strategy, business interactions and logistics exchanges within the
             core economic circle have become increasingly frequent, providing solid traffic support for the main corridors and further
             enhancing the overall resilience on the demand side.

      (II)   Development strategies of the Company
             ✓    Applicable                  Not Applicable

             During the “15th Five-Year Plan” period, the Company will establish a new business structure centred on four core areas:
             investment in transportation infrastructure, operation and management of transportation networks, development and
             operation of roadside ecological resources, and investment and incubation in the transportation industry. It will further
             integrate into the broader context of the Yangtze River Delta regional integration and the building of a strong transportation
             country. The Company will deeply embed ESG principles throughout its strategic planning and operational processes, aiming
             to become a new benchmark for listed road and bridge enterprises characterised by outstanding influence, innovation-
             driven capabilities, value creation, and a strong sense of social responsibility.

           (III)   Operating plan
                   ✓    Applicable                  Not Applicable

                   1.      In 2026, the Company will adhere to the core guidance of high-quality development, uphold the overarching
                           principle of “seeking progress while maintaining stability and using progress to promote production”, focus on
                           expanding and improving its core business and the in-depth development of the road-based economy, and strive
                           to establish a new industrial structure characterised by “solid core business, optimised structure, and green, low-
                           carbon practices”.

                           Improve the layout of the road network and strengthen synergy of the road network. Focusing on optimizing
                           the layout of the road network of southern Jiangsu, the Company will build a sustainable investment return model to
                           provide solid capital support for road network structure upgrading and core business extension. With new projects
                           such as Xitai Expressway and Danjin Expressway as key drivers, the Company will strengthen synergy within the
                           core area of southern Jiangsu.

                           Deepen the digital and intelligent transformation to establish a benchmark for intelligent operations in
                           the industry. Building on the characteristics of a “high-traffic, high-saturation” road network, the Company will
                           iterate smart transportation solutions and deeply integrate traffic forecasting and dynamic guidance technologies.
                           This will enhance the traffic efficiency of core road sections during peak hours, achieving steady growth in toll
                           revenue and precise reduction in management and maintenance costs.

                           Cultivate the “Transportation+" ecosystem to drive the platform-based transformation of road-related
                           economy. Centred on travel services, the Company will promote the transformation of service areas into integrated
                           cultural and tourism platforms. It will deeply explore land, traffic flow, and scenario resources along the routes, with
                           a focus on developing the “transportation-energy integration” and “transportation-tourism integration” business
                           models, to build a highly cohesive road-related industrial ecosystem.

                           Forge first-mover advantages in ESG and cultivate new driving forces for green development. With
                           full integration of the ESG management system into governance processes, the Company establish industry
                           benchmarks on key issues to enhance the capital market profile. Leveraging the clean energy business, the
                           Company will accelerate the deployment of distributed photovoltaic and energy storage systems along the road
                           assets. By actively exploring forward-looking businesses such as electricity market trading, the Company will
                           change the green and low-carbon transformation from a “social responsibilities” into “operational dividends”.

(IV)   Possible risks
       ✓    Applicable                  Not Applicable

       According to the macro environment and the current business situation, the Group will mainly face the following risks:

       1.      Risks associated with industry policies

               Risk analysis: The Group is primarily engaged in the investment, construction, operations and management of toll
               roads and bridges, and toll road income are the major source for the Group at present. The adjustment and change
               of industry policies, national macro-control policies and tax policies will directly or indirectly affect the Group’s
               business revenue and thus the Group is exposed to the operating risks brought by industry policies.

               Countermeasures: To address policy risks, the Group will pay close attention to the development of relevant
               policies and research on policy trends. It will establish a dynamic policy risk tracking and assessment mechanism
               and enhance the contact and communication with the relevant government authorities, especially transportation,
               financial, taxation and pricing departments so that it can adjust its business decisions accordingly in a timely manner
               and develop new profit growth points to reduce pressure on toll road income. Meanwhile, it actively explores the
               layout of industrial upgrading and development around the main business of road and bridge, builds a diversified
               profit model, and strengthens the Group’s risk-resistant ability and sustainable development momentum.

       2.      Risks associated with changes in competition patterns

               Risk analysis: As the expressway network is improved gradually, the industry faces more fierce competition. The
               opening of roads and bridges with substitution effects may reduce the market share and growth in revenue of the
               Group. With the on-going expansion of railway network in Jiangsu Province, the existing market share of the Group
               will be squeezed, which will affect the future development of the principal business of the Group.

               Countermeasures: The Group will establish high-quality traffic condition and road appearance to create a
               comfortable travelling environment and establish a sound brand image. It will construct a coordinated platform
               for road network operations to improve the sharing and control of road information as well as service quality.
               Additionally, it will promote the construction of “intelligent expressways” to explore 5G application scenarios and
               increase the dependence of drivers and passengers on the roads of the Group. Meanwhile, the Group will pay close
               attention to regional planning for the road network and formulate strategies to respond to different situations in a
               timely manner and enhance contingency capabilities.

       3.      Risks associated with project investment

               Risk analysis: The Group’s road and bridge projects under construction and new road and bridge projects are
               subject to economic, political and related factors, and there is a risk that the future returns may fall short of
               expectations. In addition, investment in financial and quasi-financial products may involve risks of losses and gains
               due to market fluctuations and systematic risks.

               Countermeasures: The Group will improve the mechanisms for introducing and cultivating professionals, improve its
               project research capability, strengthen forward-looking judgment, and raise the probability of successful investment.
               Furthermore, it will reinforce the internal control measures for external investment, establish reasonable procedures
               for decision-making, strengthen post-investment management and lower the probability of investment risks.




                                                                                                                2025 Annual Repor t       49
     REPORT OF THE BOARD




                     4.        Risks associated with a lower-than-expected rate of destocking

                               Risk analysis: Due to its long industry chain and cycle, the real estate sector is susceptible to changes in market
                               environment and policies. Economic operation environment, changes in fiscal and monetary policies and the policies
                               for taming the real estate market may affect the sales cycle and sales performance of the Group’s real estate
                               business, leading to an extension of the property sales cycle, affecting the progress of destocking and exit of real
                               state funds.

                               Countermeasures: The Group will establish a risk management system and a normalised risk appraisal mechanism,
                               stay up-to-date with policies concerning the industry and the development of the macro-economy and the industry
                               and integrate risk management into real estate projects. Besides, it will reinforce the specialised management
                               of projects, build up its capability to gain insights into government policy and market development trends, shift
                               business strategies, partially serve the transformation and upgrading of the main business, adopt effective
                               preventive measures, and step up efforts to accelerate destocking so as to intensify the control of real state funds
                               and take multiple measures to minimize risks.

     I.    DETAILS OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE OF THE COMPANY
            ✓   Applicable                 Not Applicable

           The Group adheres to the philosophy of integrity and diligence, is committed to excellent corporate governance, and continuously
           improves the corporate governance mechanism of “clear powers and responsibilities, separate functions, effective balancing and
           coordinated operation” for shareholders, the board of directors and the management in accordance with the laws and regulations
           of the two places and the listing rules and other regulations. It continuously optimizes the corporate institutions, decision-
           making institutions, executive agencies, and supervisory agencies, focuses on the establishment of a standardized information
           disclosure mechanism, As the standing body of the Company, the Board of Directors exercises all powers not reserved for the
           shareholders’ meeting under the “Articles of Association”. It exercises management and decision-making authority in accordance
           with the “Procedural Rules for the Board of Directors” in areas such as corporate development strategy, management structure,
           investment and financing, planning, financial monitoring, and personnel matters. The management is responsible for organising and
           implementing the resolutions of the shareholders’ meeting and the board of directors, and for presiding over the daily operational
           management of the Company. In addition, the Company focuses on establishing a standardised information disclosure mechanism,
           a smooth investor communication mechanism and a robust investor return mechanism, actively fulfills its responsibilities to
           stakeholders including shareholders, customers, employees and the society, and strives to build an excellent enterprise in the
           expressway industry.

           Throughout the Reporting Period, the corporate governance situation of the Group was in compliance with the requirements
           outlined by the Company Law (《公司法》), the Securities Law (《證券法》), and the normative documents on corporate governance
           of listed companies issued by the CSRC and the SSE. The Group strictly adhered to the guidelines laid out in the Corporate
           Governance Code, Appendix C1 of the Hong Kong Listing Rules, and implemented the recommended best practices outlined in
           the aforementioned code. The Company, the Board of Directors of the Company, directors, and senior management have not been
           subject to administrative punishment, notice of criticism, or public reprimand by the regulatory authorities.

           During the Reporting Period, the Group’s corporate governance was widely acknowledged by the capital market and various sectors
           of society. The Group was awarded the “2025 National Advanced Collective in the Transportation System”, the “Pegasus Award
           for Investor Relations and Shareholder Return of Chinese Listed Companies”, the “China Listed Companies Yinghua A-Share Value
           Demonstration Case”, and the “2025 Shareholder Return Golden Bull Award”. It was also honoured in the Hong Kong stock market
           with the “China Listed Companies Yinghua Hong Kong Share Value Demonstration Case”.

           Whether there is any significant difference between the requirements of the corporate governance of the Company and the
           provisions of laws, administrative regulations and the relevant regulations of the China Securities Regulatory Commission on the
           governance of listed companies; if there is a significant difference, the reason should be explained.

     II.   SPECIFIC MEASURES TAKEN BY THE CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDER AND THE DE
           FACTO CONTROLLER OF THE COMPANY TO ENSURE THE INDEPENDENCE OF THE
           COMPANY’S ASSETS, PERSONNEL, FINANCE, ORGANIZATION AND BUSINESS,
           AND SOLUTIONS, WORK PROGRESS AND FOLLOW-UP WORK PLANS ADOPTED
           WHEN THE INDEPENDENCE OF THE COMPANY IS AFFECTED
            ✓   Applicable                 Not Applicable

           Based on the principle of “distinctive ownership, clearly defined powers and responsibilities”, the Company and its Controlling
           Shareholders, are independent of each other in terms of operations, assets, personnel, organization and finance. The Company and
           its controlling shareholder have a pure property-based relationship, with separate business scopes and no upstream-downstream
           relationship. Although there is some objective competition between the Company and its controlling shareholder due to their
           partially overlapping business operations, it has not significantly affected the Company’s normal business operations. The Company
           has complete ownership of its operating assets and operates independently from its controlling shareholder. There is no cross-
           employment between the two entities, and the Company has autonomy in making decisions regarding labor, personnel, and salary
           management. Candidates recommended by the controlling shareholder for the board of directors of the Company undergo a strict
           review process by the Company’s nomination committee, remuneration and appraisal committee, and board of directors. There is
           no “two signs, one team,” mixed ownership, or co-office situations in the organization, and the office and operating locations are
           separate. The Company has an independent finance department, with its own accounts and the ability to make independent financial
           decisions, without interference from the controlling shareholder.

                  2.     Shareholder rights

                         (1)      Shareholders’ right to convene an extraordinary general meeting or special general meeting.

                                   In accordance with the Articles of Association, shareholders individually or in aggregate holding a total of
                                   10% or more of the shares of the Company have the right to request in writing to the board of directors to
                                   convene an extraordinary general meeting, and such request shall be submitted to the Board of Directors
                                   in writing. The Board of Directors shall, in compliance with the laws, administrative regulations and these
                                   Articles of Association, provide a written response indicating its agreement or disagreement to convene the
                                   extraordinary general meeting within 10 days after receipt of the request. If the Board of Directors agrees
                                   to convene an extraordinary general meeting, it shall issue a notice convening such meeting within 5 days
                                   after it has so resolved. Any changes to the original request in the notice shall be subject to the consent of
                                   the relevant shareholders. If the Board of Directors disagrees to convene an extraordinary general meeting,
                                   or fails to provide any response within 10 days upon receipt of the request, the holders of ordinary shares
                                   (including preference shareholders with voting rights restored) holding, individually or collectively, 10% or
                                   more of the voting shares of the Company are entitled to propose to the Audit Committee the convening
                                   of an extraordinary general meeting, and such proposal shall be submitted to the Audit Committee in
                                   writing. If the Audit Committee consents to convene an extraordinary general meeting, it shall issue a
                                   notice for convening the general meeting within five days upon receipt of the request. Any changes to
                                   the original request in the notice shall be subject to the consent of the relevant shareholders. If the Audit
                                   Committee fails to issue a notice for convening the general meeting within the prescribed period, it shall be
                                   deemed that the Audit Committee does not convene and chair the general meeting, in which case ordinary
                                   shareholders (including preference shareholders with restored voting rights) who individually or collectively
                                   hold 10% or more of the voting shares of the Company for 90 consecutive days or more may convene
                                   and chair the meeting of their own accord. The procedures for convening the meeting shall, to the extent
                                   possible, be the same as those for convening a general meeting by the Board of Directors.




54   Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited

 (2)   Shareholders’ rights and protocols for presenting resolutions at the Shareholders’ general meetings

       In accordance with the Articles of Association, shareholders individually or collectively holding over 1%
       of the total voting Shares of the Company have the right to submit proposals to the Company. Any
       shareholder, either individually or jointly holding more than 1% of the Company’s shares, may submit
       a temporary proposal in writing to the convener, i.e., the board of directors. Such a proposal must be
       submitted 10 days before the shareholders’ meeting is scheduled to take place. The submission should be
       addressed to Ms. CHEN Jinjia (the secretary of the board of directors), at No. 6, Xianlin Avenue, Nanjing,
       Jiangsu Province, China. A supplemental notice shall be issued by the convener within 2 days after receipt
       of such proposals. Save as prescribed above, the convener shall not revise the proposals stated in the
       notice of shareholders’ general meetings nor add in new proposals after issuing the notice of general
       meeting. The Company shall place the proposal on the agenda for the said meeting if the said proposal falls
       within the functions and powers of general meetings.

 (3)   Shareholders’ right to questioning procedure

       Pursuant to the Article 8.3(iii) of the Articles of Association, shareholders have the right to raise inquiries as
       to business and operational activities of the Company. The relevant members of the Board of Directors or
       the senior management shall attend the general meeting to receive the inquiries and make corresponding
       responses or explanations regarding the questions and recommendations of the shareholders.

       Shareholders are also able to submit written inquiries and express their opinions to the Board of Directors
       through the Secretary’s Office at any time. The following are the contact details for the Secretary’s Office
       of the Board of Directors:

       Address: No. 6, Xianlin Avenue,
       Email: jsnh@jsexpwy.com
       Telephone: 8625–84362700 ext. 301815
       Fax: 8625–84207788

       The Office of the Secretary to the Board of Directors of the Company handles queries made by shareholders
       of the Company via telephone and in writing from time to time. Where appropriate, the queries and opinions
       of shareholders will be forwarded to the board of directors and/or relevant committees under the board of
       directors of the Company to answer the queries raised by the shareholders. Shareholders are entitled to
       obtain relevant information including the Articles of Association, all and any branch register of members,
       personal information of directors, managers and other senior management members of the Company.
