            (II)      During the Reporting Period, the Audit Committee held 9 meetings

                      The Audit Committee was established in 2001. Its current members comprise 4 directors. The convenor is Mr. XU
                      Guanghua*, an independent non-executive director. Members include Mr. YANG Shaojun, Mr. GU Zhaoyang and Mr. SUN
                      Lijun. There are 1 non-executive director and 3 independent non-executive directors.

                      *     Mr. Xu Guanghua, an independent non-executive director, possesses the appropriate professional qualifications or appropriate accounting
                            or relevant financial management expertise as required under Rule 3.10(2) of Hong Kong Listing Rules.


                      The Audit Committee is principally responsible for reviewing and monitoring the quality and procedures of the Company’s
                      financial reporting and supervising the establishment and implementation of the Company’s internal audit system;
                      examining the financial information of the Company and its subsidiaries and its disclosure; reviewing the establishment of
                      the Company’s internal control system and supervising its implementation, including financial control and other aspects;
                      auditing major related party/connected transactions of the Company; and communicating, supervising and reviewing the
                      work of the internal and external auditors of the Company.

                      During the Reporting Period, the Audit Committee held a total of 9 meetings, including 4 periodic report meetings and 2
                      separate communication meetings with external audit institutions. It reviews the Company’s periodic reports; reviews related
                      party/connected transactions, supervises and evaluates the external audit work, selects external auditors; reviews the
                      internal control system, supervises and guides internal audits, promotes internal and external audit findings and rectification;
                      strengthens internal control supervision and evaluation; reviews and monitors the Company’s financial reporting quality
                      and procedures; and provides support for the Board of Directors’ decision-making on the above matters, and puts forward
                      important opinions and suggestions. Please refer to the table below for matters discussed at each separate meeting.

                      According to the working rules of the annual report, the Audit Committee reviews the Company’s annual financial
                      report, and fully communicates with the management and forms written opinions before the commencement of on-site
                      work of external auditors; for the preliminary audit opinions issued by the external auditors, the committee strengthens
                      communication with the external auditors. It reviews and communicates the annual financial report again; after the
                      completion the audit of the annual financial report, the Audit Committee reviews and votes, and submits to the Board of
                      Directors for review.

(III)   During the Reporting Period, the Nomination Committee held 2 meetings

        The Nomination, Remuneration and Appraisal Committee established by the Company in 2001 was split into the Nomination
        Committee and the Remuneration and Appraisal Committee in 2012 as required by the Stock Exchange. Its current
        members comprise 5 directors. The convenor is Mr. SUN Lijun, an independent non-executive director. Members include
        Ms. XIE Mengmeng, Mr. YANG Shaojun, Mr. XU Guanghua and Mr. GE Yang. There are 2 non-executive directors and 3
        independent non-executive directors.

        The Nomination Committee is primarily responsible for studying the Company’s human resources development strategies
        and plans, and for reviewing and making recommendations regarding the candidates, qualifications, selection criteria, and
        appointment procedures for directors and members of senior management. The Nomination Committee comprehensively
        considers various factors such as skills, knowledge, experience, gender, age, cultural and educational background, and
        widely identifies individuals with suitable qualifications to serve as directors and senior management personnel within
        the Company, its controlling (shareholding) enterprises, and the talent market. It collects information on the candidates’
        professional background, academic qualifications, professional titles, detailed work experience, and all concurrent positions,
        compiling written materials. The Committee convenes meetings to review the qualifications of the shortlisted candidates
        based on the appointment criteria for directors and senior management personnel. One to two months prior to the election
        of new directors and the appointment of new senior management personnel, it submits recommendations and relevant
        materials regarding director candidates and new senior management appointees to the Board of Directors.

        The Nomination Committee held 2 meetings during the Reporting Period. The Nomination Committee reviews the
        qualifications of directors, evaluates the structure, number and composition of the Board of Directors, and pays attention
        to the improvement of diversity. As of the date of this report, there are 12 members of the eleventh session of the Board
        of Directors of the Company, including one executive director and six non-executive directors. Five of the non-executive
        directors were appointed by the Company externally, including one who is a well-known person in Hong Kong, and five
        independent non-executive directors, which guarantees sufficient independence of the Board of Directors. The Board of
        Directors is comprised of persons at different ages and with different work experience and academic background, including
        one female director, which guarantees the diversity of the board members, which helps the board analyze and discuss
        issues from multiple perspectives. The Nomination Committee places emphasis on the development and cultivation of senior
        management and succession talent. For changes in senior management and certain professional staff, the Committee
        comprehensively evaluates candidates’ educational background, professional qualifications, experience, and independence,
        follows the relevant nomination procedures, and submits the candidates to the Board for review after deliberation by the
        Nomination Committee. The appointment of the proposed senior management and professional staff takes effect upon
        review and approval by the Board. For information on the gender ratio of all employees (including senior management) of
        the Company, please see the disclosure under “(I) Staff profile” of “V. Details of Staff of the Parent Company and Its Major
        Subsidiaries at the End of the Reporting Period”.

        The Board of Directors of the Company has adopted a set of board diversity policy, which sets out the approach to
        achieving board diversity. In considering the diversity of board members, the Company will take into account a number
        of aspects, including but not limited to gender, age, cultural and educational background, professional experience, skills,
        knowledge and tenure of service to achieve board diversity. Under the board diversity policy, the Committee continues to
        cultivate and seek talents that promote board diversity, building up a talent pool of potential director successors. All board
        appointments consider candidates on the basis of merit and contribution and objective conditions, and carefully consider
        the benefits of board diversity. The Nomination Committee regularly reviews the policy to discuss whether any amendments
        are necessary and to recommend to the Board of Directors any such amendments for consideration and approval.

        After reviewing the board diversity policy and the composition of the Board of Directors, the Nomination Committee is
        satisfied that all the requirements set out in the diversification policy have been met.

                  honesty, diligence and due care, and had conscientiously honoured their service contracts. They devoted the requisite
                  attention and sufficient time to the Company’s affairs, fully leveraging their professional expertise and experience to assist
                  the Board in making scientific and efficient decisions, thereby ensuring the realisation of the Company’s best interests. The
                  Company’s management demonstrated professionalism and commitment, successfully accomplishing the various annual
                  operational and management objectives set by the Board at the beginning of the year. The committee has examined the
                  remuneration information of the directors, supervisors and senior management disclosed by the Company in this annual

                  management of the Company held any shares, share options or being granted restricted shares of the Company, and
                  currently, the Company has not adopted any share incentive schemes.

                  The committee has approved the terms of the service contract of executive directors and ensured that none of the directors
                  or any of their associates participated in the determination of their own remuneration.

                  The primary responsibilities of the Strategy Committee are to review and assess the Company’s strategic development
                  direction, study and provide recommendations on major capital operations, asset management projects, and investment
                  and financing plans, formulate the Company’s strategic plans, monitor the implementation of strategies, improve investment
                  decision-making processes to enhance the scientific nature of decision-making, increase the efficiency and quality of major
                  investment decisions, and conduct independent reviews of the quality and efficiency of risk management work.

                  structure, improved asset returns and capital efficiency, strengthened the Company’s compliance awareness, enhanced
                  risk management and anti-fraud work, and elevated the capability to serve the real economy. For the performance of the
                  Strategy Committee in assessing and reviewing risk management work, please refer to “2. On internal audit management
                  and internal control and risk management”, Section XV. Others of this chapter.

(II)    Remuneration policy
        ✓    Applicable                   Not Applicable

        During the Reporting Period, the Group thoroughly implemented the deployment requirements for state-owned enterprise
        reform, closely integrated with the practical realities of the road and bridge industry, and continued to deepen the reform of
        the remuneration management mechanism. The Group comprehensively implemented the “position-based remuneration,
        performance-based remuneration” distribution mechanism, effectively stimulating the vitality of employees in pursuing
        business and innovation.

        By establishing and refining a diversified incentive system encompassing remuneration incentives, performance evaluation,
        and welfare benefits, the Group has effectively mobilised the enthusiasm, initiative, and creativity of its employees.
        During the Reporting Period, the total employee compensation amounted to approximately RMB917.4517 million, which
        genuinely reflects the Group’s full respect for and reasonable return on the value of its employees. Concurrently, the Group
        actively built a platform for talent development, promoting multi-position experience and multi-dimensional enhancement
        for employees through various means such as secondments, shadowing programmes, and talent recruitment, thereby
        comprehensively strengthening their professional capabilities and overall competencies. During the Reporting Period, the
        Group cultivated and recruited a group of high-quality talents, injecting new momentum into high-quality development and
        fostering a positive environment that “respects talent, encourages innovation, and supports growth”.

        Moving forward, the Group will continue to deepen the reform of talent development systems and mechanisms, continuously
        expand career development opportunities, and improve mechanisms for talent cultivation, recruitment, utilisation, and
        motivation, thereby providing robust talent support and intellectual assurance for the Group’s sustained and healthy
        development.

(III)   Training programs
        ✓    Applicable                   Not Applicable

        As the 14th Five-Year Plan draws to a close, employees, as the core force driving the Group’s operational development,
        play a crucial role in achieving the Group’s strategic objectives, with their quality and capability enhancement being
        of paramount importance. Aligned with its development plans, talent requirements, and the actual composition of its
        workforce, the Group adheres to the principles of tailored training and practical effectiveness. It has meticulously established
        a multi-tiered and hierarchical comprehensive training system covering senior management, middle-level and supervisory
        personnel, newly promoted managers, and grassroots young key employees. On one hand, the Group organises training
        for the management team to instil new development concepts, foster new development paradigms, balance the relationship
        between reform, development, and stability, and lead the enterprise towards high-quality development. It also arranges
        competency training for middle-level and key management personnel in batches, drawing on best practices from benchmark
        enterprises to enhance management efficiency and decision-making capabilities. On the other hand, the Group conducts
        capability enhancement training for dispatchers and toll collectors, focusing on the operational areas of team leaders,
        grassroots, and maintenance management personnel to improve employees’ professional competence and technical
        skills. It places particular emphasis on organising certification training for safety and specialised operations personnel,
        ensuring a 100% certification rate for relevant positions. In response to the national strategy for skilled talent, the Group
        provides comprehensive training for all technical positions, achieving full certification, and offers specialised training for
        drone operators. During the Reporting Period, the Group invested approximately RMB13,796,800 in training, covering
        employees at all levels. This systematic training programme has strengthened employees’ sense of responsibility, enhanced
        their comprehensive capabilities, and improved the talent team empowerment construction, thereby providing robust talent
        support and intellectual assurance for the Group’s sustainable and rapid development during the concluding year of the
        14th Five-Year Plan and beyond.

VIII. BUILDING OF INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION DURING
      THE REPORTING PERIOD
      ✓    Applicable                   Not Applicable

      During the Reporting Period, the Company continued to strengthen its internal control system, focusing on key areas such as legal
      compliance, risk management, and quality management. It systematically advanced the improvement of institutional processes,
      comprehensively enhancing the standard of corporate governance and the capacity for risk prevention.

      First, the Company has implemented the comprehensive optimisation of the coordinated operation mechanism for major
      risk control. The institutional framework centred on the “Major Risk Control Guidelines” was further refined. The “Regulations on
      the Management of Rules and Systems” and a series of accountability systems for violations in operational investment were issued.
      A review of 307 existing systems was completed, and a plan for streamlining and strengthening the framework was formulated.
      Concurrently, rules of procedure for major risk control discussions, a mandatory consultation mechanism, and a parallel review
      process for significant operational risks were established, achieving thorough monitoring and refined management in key areas.

      Second, the Company systematically advanced the development of the regulatory framework and internal control
      system. The Company has revised and issued the “Detailed Rules for Contract Management”, updated 32 types of commonly used
      contract templates, and strengthened the foundation for business compliance. It comprehensively carried out the “establishment,
      revision, abolition, and interpretation” of regulatory documents. During the Reporting Period, six new regulations were formulated, 22
      were revised, and eight were abolished. The compilation of the “List of Positional Compliance Responsibilities” for 46 modules was
      completed, and the compilation of the 2026 edition of the company’s regulatory documents and the “Internal Control Manual” was
      initiated, further enhancing the uniformity, applicability, and enforceability of the regulatory framework.

      Third, the Company deepened risk identification and control alongside digital transformation. It established a
      comprehensive risk control system in key areas such as “major decisions, significant personnel appointments, important projects,
      and large-sum fund operations”, contract management, and bidding and procurement, achieving transparent monitoring and refined
      management. Leveraging the “Digital Jiangsu Expressway” platform, the Company has promoted the optimisation of the risk control
      information system by business and module, refined the application of risk checklists across seven domains and 21 categories, and
      enhanced capabilities in risk early warning and precise control.

IX.   MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL OF SUBSIDIARIES DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD
      ✓    Applicable                   Not Applicable

      During the Reporting Period, the Company continued to refine the approval procedures for subsidiary proposals, further clarifying
      approval authorities and standardising the submission process. This has established a comprehensive, multi-layered control
      framework spanning from management decision-making to business execution, thereby continuously enhancing the risk prevention
      and control capabilities as well as governance effectiveness of its subsidiaries. Meanwhile, the initial deployment of risk monitoring
      platform built around investment sectors was completed with the trial operation stage initiated. Focusing on core sectors such
      as road and bridge business, finance, transportation and energy integration, and subsidiary management, the Company used
      information technology to systematically carry out information collection, dynamic monitoring, intelligent early warning and regular
      reporting of risk events, and promoted the extension of risk management from post-event handling to pre-event prevention
      and in-event control, further improving the timeliness and accuracy of risk response. Furthermore, in strict compliance with the
      requirements of the “Subsidiary Management Measures” imposed by the Company, subsidiaries at all levels submitted monthly
      reports on the progress of major projects, business operations, and key financial indicators. Based on this, the Company conducted
      multi-dimensional consolidation, analysis, and assessment, providing regularised support for the timely identification of potential

     XII.   ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION OF LISTED COMPANIES AND THEIR MAJOR
            SUBSIDIARIES INCLUDED IN THE ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATION DISCLOSURE
            LIST IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE LAW
                  Applicable              ✓   Not Applicable

            Other explanations

            According to the “2025 Nanjing Corporate Environmental Information Disclosure List,” the Group is not included among the
            enterprises required to disclose environmental information in accordance with the law. During the Reporting Period, the Company
            strictly complied with laws, regulations and rules such as the “Environmental Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China,”
            the “Environmental Protection Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China,” the “Energy Conservation Law of the People’s
            Republic of China,” the “Water and Soil Conservation Law of the People’s Republic of China,” the “Soil Pollution Prevention
            and Control Law of the People’s Republic of China,” and the “Jiangsu Province Energy Conservation Regulations”. The
            Company has improved its environmental management system, strengthened the bottom line for environmental risks, reduced
            pollution emissions, and no environmental violation penalties occurred.

            (I)      Information on emission

                     The Group has formulated the “Detailed Rules for the Management of ‘Three Wastes’", comprehensively reviewing
                     and identifying the four major categories of pollution sources–waste gas, wastewater, solid waste, and noise–in the main
                     business operations of its affiliated units. All units strictly comply with national and local environmental protection laws and
                     regulations to ensure stable and compliant discharge of various pollutants.

                     In terms of exhaust emission reduction: High priority is attached to the control and management of waste gas to
                     mitigate the impact of waste gas emissions on the surrounding environment. We have taken measures to enhance the
                     greening construction and daily maintenance of roadbed slopes and the outer sides of the side ditch to effectively alleviate
                     the pollution from vehicle exhaust on air quality along the routes. Continuous efforts were also made to ensure that the
                     roads are unobstructed, promote non-stop tolling, effectively shorten the idling time of vehicles, and thus reduce the total
                     amount of exhaust emissions. Meanwhile, kitchens in all office and service premises are equipped with oil fume purification
                     and discharge devices that comply with the “Emission Standard for Cooking Fume” (GB18483–2001). These devices are
                     maintained to operate stably and undergo regular cleaning to ensure compliant discharge of oil fumes.




94   Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited
           CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY




        In terms of sewage treatment: The relevant national laws and regulations on sewage treatment are strictly enforced, and
        a sound sewage treatment management system is established. Integrated underground sewage treatment equipment have
        been constructed and put into operation to ensure clean discharge of sewage and minimise the impact on the surrounding
        environment through advanced processes. Regular maintenance and inspection of wastewater treatment facilities are
        carried out in accordance with specifications to ensure stable and efficient operation of the equipment. Continuous efforts
        are made to strengthen the treatment of domestic sewage and the monitoring and control of water quality. For stations with
        suitable conditions, production and domestic sewage are connected to the municipal sewage network for unified treatment.
        For stations without access to such networks, treated water that meets the standards is reused for greening and irrigation,
        achieving the recycling of water resources. During the Reporting Period, sewage discharge complied with the standards.

        In terms of noise reduction: Priority is given to the use of low-noise road surface materials as the primary noise reduction
        method to fundamentally reduce noise generation. Combined with the characteristics of the project and the surrounding
        natural environment, the green isolation belt is scientifically designed to build an ecological noise barrier, effectively blocking
        the spread of noise. Key nodes such as dense road sections and parallel roads are accurately set up with sound barrier
        facilities to form a three-dimensional sound insulation protection system. Highway operating vehicle alarm devices are
        replaced with directional horns to control the sound range and direction. If the active control measures still fail to meet the
        quality standards for outdoor sound environment, passive protection facilities such as sound insulation windows will be used
        in due course to ensure that noise pollution is effectively controlled. During the Reporting Period, noise emissions complied
        with standards.

        In terms of waste disposal: A comprehensive waste management system was established, implementing tracking
        statistics and closed-loop management for the entire process of waste generation, recycling, and disposal. The requirements
        for segregated storage of hazardous solid waste were strictly implemented, with enhanced daily supervision and control to
        ensure safe and compliant disposal; the use of chemical products explicitly prohibited by the state was resolutely prohibited,
        and environmentally friendly products and services were prioritised. Equal emphasis was placed on source reduction and
        resource utilisation. Waste generation was effectively reduced through optimised management processes, and the reuse,
        recycling, and recovery of waste were actively promoted. Qualified professional institutions were engaged for the recycling
        and disposal of hazardous waste, achieving efficient resource utilisation. The Company incorporated waste management
        into the quarterly inspection and assessment system to ensure the effective implementation of all control measures. During
        the Reporting Period, the Company achieved a 100% recycling rate for waste materials such as waste asphalt residue was
        100%, and the utilization rate of low-carbon maintenance materials such as seam tape and pouring sealant was 100%.

(II)    Emergency plan for environmental emergencies

        The Company has formulated the “Detailed Rules for Emergency Management of Environmental Contingencies”,
        standardising the emergency management procedures for environmental incidents. In addition, it has established an
        Emergency Response Leading Group for Environmental Incidents, with a subordinate Emergency Rescue Office, to
        coordinate and conduct emergency response and environmental management for environmental incidents. The Company
        regularly conducted ecological and environmental hidden danger inspections, emergency plan filing and management, and
        organized daily emergency drills. It systematically identified various environmental risks including water pollution accidents,
        air pollution accidents, noise and vibration pollution accidents, solid waste pollution accidents and toxic chemical pollution
        accidents. During the Reporting Period, no environmental incidents occurred at the Company, and environmental safety
        remained stable and controllable.

(III)   Environmental protection self-testing plan

        The Group implemented a three-tier environmental protection management system at the corporate, secondary unit,
        and grassroots unit levels, continuously enhancing environmental monitoring capabilities. The Group has streamlined
        its environmental protection institutional framework, strictly enforced the implementation of regulations, deepened
        environmental education and specialised training for construction personnel, and focused on key areas such as ecological
        protection, construction noise, and dust control. It has scientifically formulated environmental monitoring plans, regularly
        conducted wastewater discharge testing and noise monitoring in sensitive areas, diligently maintained road drainage
        systems and protected water sources, thereby strengthening the ecological security barrier.

           (V)    Implementation of other environmental responsibilities

                  During the Reporting Period, Ninghu Expressway adhered to the green development philosophy, systematically advancing
                  ecological and environmental protection in the construction, operation, management, and maintenance of expressways. The

                  advocates low-carbon and intensive operations, and embeds the concept of emission reduction into daily management; it
                  attaches great importance to the protection of biodiversity along the routes, and promotes the harmonious coexistence of
                  humans and nature.

                  Green maintenance: The Group continues to drive the green development of road maintenance and deeply integrates
                  the control of environmental impact indicators into the entire life cycle of major and minor repair maintenance. The Group
                  further advances the circular utilization of resources, promotes the on-site hot recycling technology for pavement in light of
                  local conditions, and realizes the recycling of old pavement materials by adding recycling agents and new materials. The
                  Group has innovated its green operation model, deployed eco-friendly mechanical snow removal equipment such as snow
                  blowers and snow plows, and replaced traditional chemical snow-melting agents, effectively avoiding chemical corrosion
                  to bridge and road structures and the surrounding ecology. Environmentally friendly materials are adopted, and renewable
                  low-carbon maintenance materials such as joint tapes and crack sealing adhesives are promoted and applied to fully build a new
                  eco-friendly benchmark for road maintenance.

                  Green office practices: In terms of hardware energy conservation, energy-efficient equipment has been popularized and
                  refined energy consumption management and control implemented; in terms of resource intensification, paperless office
                  work has been vigorously promoted, and the procurement and collection procedures for office supplies have been strictly
                  standardized to cut resource waste from the source; in terms of low-carbon commuting, employees are encouraged to
                  prioritize public transportation, effectively reducing commuting carbon footprints. Simultaneously, the Company regularly
                  conducted diversified environmental activities such as afforestation, World Environment Day education, and waste clean-up
                  campaigns to enhance employees’ environmental awareness and social responsibility.

                  Biodiversity protection: The Company has adopted relatively comprehensive drainage, protection and greening measures.
                  Since the commissioning of the highway, various soil and water conservation measures have started to play their role,
                  and soil erosion in the road area has been effectively controlled. The cultural landscapes and natural environment along
                  the highway have been enhanced, with greening upgrades carried out in central medians, interchange areas, toll stations,
                  service areas, embankment slopes, and other vegetable zones along the route, resulting in a notable overall improvement in
                  the greening effect of the corridor.

                   2.     On internal audit management and internal control and risk management

                          Currently, the Company has established the risk management and internal control systems. During the year, the
                          Company’s internal audit department, Strategy Committee and external independent auditor conducted preliminary
                          review, rectification, audit and evaluation of the effectiveness of the establishment and implementation of the
                          risk management and internal control systems respectively, and ensured that a comprehensive audit covering all
                          businesses and management activities under risk management and internal control was carried out each year.

                          The Board of Directors of the Company acknowledges that it shall be responsible for the risk management and
                          internal control systems and review their effectiveness annually. The risk management and internal control systems
                          of the Company are designed to manage rather than eliminate the risk of failure to achieve business goals. There is
                          only reasonable but not absolute assurance that material misrepresentations or losses can be avoided. The Board
                          of Directors (including independent non-executive directors) has considered the opinions offered by the Strategy
                          Committee, reviewed the risk management and internal control systems of the Group and is of the view that such
                          systems are effective and adequate.

                          The Company has taken into consideration the resources, staff qualifications and experience in corporate
                          accounting and internal auditing in reviewing the risk management and internal control matters. The Company
                          has sufficient resources to support financial reporting. The relevant employees also possess the qualifications and
                          experience required for their positions and have the opportunity to receive targeted professional training each year.

                          The Company has created a dedicated internal audit department to audit the Company’s risk management and
                          internal control systems. In addition, the Company’s internal audit department and external independent auditor
                          also conduct a comprehensive audit each year to recognize, assess and manage material risks, review the
                          effectiveness of the Company’s risk management and internal control systems, and resolve serious internal control
                          errors. Save as described in paragraph 1 headed “On management of inside information” above, the Company
                          also deals with and publishes inside information and internal control measures through Office of the Secretary to the
                          Board from time to time during the year.

                   6.     Explanations regarding the Company enabling holders of its securities to obtain tax relief

                          (1)    A Shares

                                 For individual shareholders (including securities investment funds) holding the Company’s A Shares, in
                                 accordance with the relevant provisions of the Notice on Issues Concerning the Differentiated Individual
                                 Income Tax Policy on Dividend Income from Listed Companies (Caishui [2015] No. 101) and the Notice on
                                 Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Differentiated Individual Income Tax Policy on Dividend Income
                                 from Listed Companies (Caishui [2012] No. 85): for a shareholding period exceeding one year, dividend
                                 income is temporarily exempt from individual income tax; for a shareholding period of one month or less
                                 the full amount of dividend income is included in taxable income; for a shareholding period of more than
                                 one month to one year (including one year), 50% of the dividend income is temporarily included in taxable
                                 income. The above income is uniformly subject to individual income tax at the rate of 20%. According to the
                                 aforementioned provisions, the Company will not withhold individual income tax when distributing dividends
                                 to individual shareholders (including securities investment funds). When such shareholders transfer their
                                 shares, China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited Shanghai Branch will calculate the
                                 tax payable based on their shareholding period. Securities companies and other share custody institutions
                                 will deduct the amount from the individual shareholders’ fund accounts and transfer it to China Securities
                                 Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited Shanghai Branch, which will then transfer it to the Company.
                                 Upon receiving the tax payment, the Company will declare and pay the tax to the competent tax authority.

                                 For qualified foreign institutional investor (QFII) shareholders holding the Company’s A Shares, in
                                 accordance with the provisions of the Notice of the State Administration of Taxation on Issues Concerning
                                 the Withholding of Enterprise Income Tax on Dividends, Bonuses and Interest Paid by Chinese Resident
                                 Enterprises to QFIIs (Guoshuihan [2009] No. 47), the Company will withhold enterprise income tax at
                                 the rate of 10%. If the relevant shareholders consider that their dividend income is eligible for treatment
                                 under a tax treaty (arrangement), they may, in accordance with regulations, apply for a tax refund from the
                                 competent tax authority on their own after receiving the dividends.

                                 For shareholders who are Hong Kong market investors (including enterprises and individuals) investing in
                                 the Company’s A Shares listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange through the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock
                                 Connect, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Notice on Tax Policies Concerning the Pilot
                                 Program for Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Market Trading Interconnection Mechanism (Caishui [2014] No.
                                 81), the Company will withhold income tax at the rate of 10%. If a “Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect”
                                 investor is a tax resident of another country and the tax treaty between that country and China stipulates a
                                 dividend withholding tax rate lower than 10%, the investor may, in accordance with regulations, apply to the
                                 competent tax authority of the Company on their own or through the withholding agent to enjoy the benefits
                                 of the tax treaty. Dividends for “Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect” investors will be distributed by the
                                 Company in RMB through China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited Shanghai Branch
                                 to the account of the nominee holder (namely, Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company Limited).

                                 For resident enterprise shareholders (including other institutional investors) holding the Company’s A-shares,
                                 the dividend withholding tax shall be paid by themselves, and the Company will not withhold or remit such
                                 tax on their behalf.




102   Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY




 (2)   H Shares

       Pursuant to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China and its Implementing
       Regulations (the “Enterprise Income Tax Law”) that have been in effect since 1 January 2008, the Company
       is obligated to withhold and pay the enterprise income tax on behalf of its non-resident enterprise
       shareholders of H shares (as defined in the Enterprise Income Tax Law, including Hong Kong Securities
       Clearing Company Limited, other corporate agents or trustees, or other organizations and groups) when
       distributing dividends, with a tax rate of 10%.

       Pursuant to the provisions of the “Notice of the State Taxation Administration on Issues Concerning the
       Withholding and Payment of Enterprise Income Tax by Chinese Resident Enterprises When Distributing
       Dividends to Non-Resident Enterprise Shareholders of Overseas H Shares” (Guoshuihan [2008] No.
       897), when a Chinese resident enterprise distributes dividends to non-resident enterprise shareholders
       of overseas H shares, it shall uniformly withhold and pay enterprise income tax at a tax rate of 10%.
       After non-resident enterprise shareholders receive dividends, they may, either by themselves, through an
       authorized agent or a withholding agent, submit an application to the competent tax authority for enjoying
       the treatment under the tax agreement (arrangement), and provide data proving that they are the actual
       beneficial owners who meet the provisions of the tax agreement (arrangement). After the competent tax
       authority verifies and confirms the relevant materials, it shall refund the difference between the tax already
       paid and the tax payable calculated in accordance with the tax rate stipulated in the tax agreement
       (arrangement).

       In accordance with the provisions of the “Notice on Tax Policies Concerning the Pilot Program of the
       Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect Mechanism” (Caishui [2014] No. 81) and the “Notice on Tax
       Policies Concerning the Pilot Program of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect Mechanism” (Caishui
       [2016] No. 127), for the dividends obtained by domestic individual investors investing in H-shares listed on
       the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong through the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect or Shenzhen-Hong
       Kong Stock Connect, the H-share companies shall withhold personal income tax at a rate of 20%. For
       dividends obtained by domestic securities investment funds from investing in shares listed on the Stock
       Exchange of Hong Kong Limited via the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect or Shenzhen-Hong Kong
       Stock Connect, individual income tax shall be levied in accordance with the aforementioned provisions. For
       domestic corporate investors investing in Hong Kong Stock Exchange-listed shares through the Shanghai-
       Hong Kong Stock Connect or Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect, H-share companies do not withhold
       enterprise income tax on dividends distributed. Domestic corporate investors are required to declare and
       pay the applicable tax on their own. Dividends received by domestic enterprises from holding H-shares
       continuously for 12 months or more are exempt from enterprise income tax in accordance with the law.

On 27 September 2024, Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable                 For details, please refer to the announcements
Energy Jiangsu Company (a wholly-owned subsidiary of YS Energy                 of the resolutions of the Board of Directors
Company (a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company)) entered into               published by the Company on the SSE website
a related party transaction agreement with Jianxing Company (an                at www.sse.com.cn on 27 September 2024
associate of the controlling shareholder of the Company), under which          and on the HKEX website at www.hkexnews.hk
Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company                on 26 September 2024, respectively.
invested in and constructed a 32.9MW distributed photovoltaic power
generation project for the whole road section of Jianchang-Xingcheng
Expressway belonging to Jianxing Company and leased the site.
According to the agreement, for the project of “Self-Generation
and Self-Consumption, with Surplus Power Feed-in” , Jiangsu
Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company shall
provide preferential tariffs to Jianxing Company in lieu of paying site rent
to Jianxing Company; and for the project of “Full Feed-in”, Jiangsu
Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company will pay
site rent to Jianxing Company. The parties will re-examine the situation
every three years to determine the annual caps for the relevant future
three years. For the project of “Self-Generation and Self-Consumption,
with Surplus Power Feed-in”, Jiangsu Communications Holding
Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company will give priority to supplying the
power generated by the photovoltaic power station project to Jianxing
Company during the agreed operation period, and provide a 15%
discount on the electricity price of the local power grid during the same
period, in lieu of paying site rent to Jianxing Company. According to
the appraisal report dated 10 July 2024 (North Asia Appraisal Report
No. [2024] No. 01-975) (the “Appraisal Report”) issued by North
Asia Assets Assessment Co., Ltd. (Special General Partnership),
the appraisal value of the annual rental for Jianchang-Xingcheng
Expressway Service Area and the side slopes held by Jianxing, which
is leased by Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable Energy
Jiangsu Company, is RMB411,453 per annum. The agreed tariff
concession of 15% is no better than the tariff concession provided by
Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company
for general industrial and commercial customers, the current general
industrial and commercial tariff is RMB0.7/kWh, the annual electricity
consumption of the premises along the Expressway is expected to be
no higher than 3,078,480 kWh per annum, and the annual reduction
of the tariff is expected to be no higher than RMB323,240.4, which
is lower than the amount of rental that would be required to be paid
if Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu
Company were to pay rent, and is not detrimental to the interests of
the Company and all of its shareholders. For the project of “Full Feed-
in”, according to the Appraisal Report, the annual rent for the side
slopes of Jianxing Expressway held by Jianxing Company, which is
leased by Jiangsu Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu
Company, is RMB456,422.82. However, in accordance with the Energy
Management Agreement, the average annual rent payable by Jiangsu
Communications Holding Renewable Energy Jiangsu Company to
Jianxing Company for the project of “Full Feed-in” is RMB280,000,
which is not higher than the amount of rent payable as calculated in
accordance with the Asset Appraisal Report.

                           Explanation of leasing

                            Huanglishu, Xianrenshan and Meicun Service Area of Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway terminated the original lease
                            contract, and the two parties signed the termination agreement, clarifying that the lease termination date for the
                            above service areas is 31 December 2021. The period between 1 January 2022 and the entry date of the new
                            lessee is a transitional period, during which the operation of those service areas would continue to be maintained
                            by the original lessee. As at the end of the Reporting Period, a new round of tendering for the aforementioned three
                            service areas had been completed. The Company collected the transitional rent from the original lessees based on
                            the newly awarded tender prices, and all transitional rent has been fully collected.

                            In November 2025, the Company entered into a lease agreement for the entire Xianrenshan Service Area with
                            Jiaxing Tonghui Expressway Service Area Management Co., Ltd., stipulating that the catering facilities would be
                            delivered first on 15 November 2025, with the retail facilities to be delivered upon the expiry of the original retail
                            contract in March 2026.

                            During the Reporting Period, the Company and its joint lessees re-evaluated the asset values related to service area
                            leases, due to the renewal of lease contracts for multiple service areas and changes in assets following the upgrade
                            and renovation of certain service areas.

          During the Reporting Period, the Company and its subsidiaries did not purchase, sale, or redeem the Company’s shares;
          no individual exercised any rights of conversion or subscription based on the convertible notes, options, warrants or any
          rights of the Company and its subsidiaries.

     2.   Right of pre-emption

          According to the Law of People’s Republic of China and the Articles of Association, the Company has no right of
          preemption to recommend about applying to shareholders for issuing new shares based on the shareholding percentage.

                   2.     Triggering and execution of issuer or investor option terms and investor protection terms

                          ✓    Applicable                   Not Applicable

                          Options for the issuer to adjust the coupon rate: An issuer is entitled to determine to adjust the coupon rate for the
                          remaining coupon period of the bonds at the end of the third year of the term of the bonds. If the issuer decides to
                          exercise the options to adjust the coupon rate, the coupon rate of the bonds shall be determined in the following
                          manner from the effective date of the adjustment: The adjusted coupon rate shall be subject to the announcement
                          of the implementation of the adjustment of the coupon rate published by the issuer, and there shall be no restriction
                          on the direction and range of the adjustment of the coupon rate. If the issuer decides not to exercise the options to
                          adjust the coupon rate, the coupon rate of the bonds shall remain unchanged until the issuer exercises the option
                          to adjust the coupon rate next time.

                          Investor’s put option: An investor is entitled to sell back all or part of the bonds held by him/her/it to the issuer at
                          the end of the third year of the term of the bonds.

                          Execution Status: During the Reporting Period, for Bond “21 NingHu G1", the issuer exercised the right to adjust
                          the coupon rate, lowering it from 3.70% to 2.93%. Investors exercised the put option, resulting in a resale amount
                          of RMB121 million for “21 NingHu G1". In accordance with the Put Implementation Announcement, the issuer may
                          resell the put bonds. Put bonds settled for this tranche: RMB121 million; Unresold bonds canceled: RMB0.

3.   Changes to the management system for information disclosure matters during the Reporting Period

     ✓   Changed                      Unchanged

      Changes to the management system for      This revision standardises terminology, replacing “Shareholders' general
      information disclosure matters              meeting(s)” with “General meeting(s)”, and assigning the audit committee
                                                  to replace the supervisory board in assuming the core responsibilities of
                                                  reviewing and supervising information disclosure. It also expands the scope
                                                  of disclosure documents and adds requirements for performance contingency
                                                  and risk disclosure. The end-to-end management of deferred/exempted
                                                  disclosures was standardised, with new supporting registration appendices
                                                  added. The disclosure responsibilities of all parties have been strengthened,
                                                  the performance requirements of directors, supervisors, senior management,
                                                  shareholders and securities service institutions have been further clarified,
                                                  the practical norms for information disclosure have been refined, and the
                                                  requirements for internal control and document preparation have been
                                                  improved.
      Main contents of the revised management   The definition of information disclosure, applicable entities, and basic principles
      system for information matters              such as truthfulness, accuracy, timeliness, and fairness have been clarified,
                                                  and new requirements such as voluntary disclosure and commitment-based
                                                  disclosure have been added. It stipulates that the disclosure content includes
                                                  periodic/interim reports, acquisition reports, etc., clarifies the standards
                                                  for performance emergency response and risk disclosure, and defines the
                                                  scope of major events and the timing of disclosure. It standardizes the
                                                  circumstances under which information disclosure is postponed/exempted,
                                                  the registration, archiving and reporting requirements, and clarifies the
                                                  disclosure process for major unprecedented matters. The board of directors
                                                  has been identified as the implementing body, the audit committee is
                                                  responsible for supervision, and the board secretary takes the lead in specific
                                                  work, clarifying the responsibilities of each party. An information compilation,
                                                  review and disclosure process has been established, the media for disclosure,
                                                  file management and confidentiality measures have been standardized, the
                                                  methods for accountability have been clarified, and three supplementary
                                                  management appendices for the postponement and exemption of certain
                                                  matters have been provided. For details, please refer to the Company’s
                                                  “Management System for Information Disclosure Matters” published on the
                                                  SSE website at www.sse.com.cn on 30 October 2025.
      Impact on investor rights                 The revised system strengthens investor rights and interests protection from
                                                  multiple dimensions, creating a more transparent and regulated information
                                                  environment for investors and safeguarding their rights to information and fair
                                                  trading.

      THE SHAREHOLDERS OF JIANGSU EXPRESSWAY COMPANY LIMITED:

      OPINION
      We have audited the accompanying financial statements of Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited (“Jiangsu Expressway”), which
      comprise the consolidated and company balance sheets as at 31 December 2025, the consolidated and company income statements, the
      consolidated and company cash flow statements, the consolidated and company statements of changes in shareholders’ equity for the year
      then ended, and notes to the financial statements.

      In our opinion, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated and company financial position
      of Jiangsu Expressway as at 31 December 2025, and the consolidated and company financial performance and cash flows of Jiangsu
      Expressway for the year then ended in accordance with Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises issued by the Ministry of Finance of
      the People’s Republic of China.

      BASIS FOR OPINION
      We conducted our audit in accordance with China Standards on Auditing for Certified Public Accountants (CSAs”). Our responsibilities under
      those standards are further described in the Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the Financial Statements section of our report. We are
      independent of the Group in accordance with the Independence Standards for Chinese Certified Public Accountants No. 1 – Independence
      Requirements for Audit and Review Engagements and the China Code of Ethics for Certified Public Accountants (“the Code”), sufficient and
      appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in accordance with the Code. We believe
      that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.

      KEY AUDIT MATTERS
      Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgement, were of most significance in our audit of the financial statements
      of the current period. These matters were addressed in the context of our audit of the financial statements as a whole, and in forming our
      opinion thereon, and we do not provide a separate opinion on these matters.

      Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement,

      Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be

I.     COMPANY STATUS
       Jiangsu Expressway Company Limited (the “Company”) is a company limited by shares established in Nanjing, Jiangsu province
       on 1 August 1992, with its head office located at Nanjing. The parent of the Company and its ultimate holding company is Jiangsu
       Communications Holding Company Limited (“Commutations Holding”).

       The principal activities of the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the “Group”) mainly include construction,
       operation and management of the Jiangsu section of Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway (the “Shanghai-Nanjing Expressway”) and
       other toll roads in Jiangsu Province, and the provision of passenger transport services and other supporting services along the toll
       road. Please refer to Note VII for details of the subsidiaries of the Company.

       During the reporting period, the information about increase in the Group’s subsidiaries is disclosed in Note VI.

II.    BASIS OF PREPARATION
       As at 31 December 2025，the Group had total current liabilities in excess of total current assets of RMB4,729,085,415.93.
       As at 31 December 2025, the Group has available unutilized bank loan facilities with a time limit over one year of not less than
       RMB10,000,000,000.00. The Company’s management believes the facilities above are to provide all necessary financial support
       to the Group in the foreseeable future so as to maintain the Group’s ability to continue as a going concern, therefore, the financial
       statements have been prepared on the going concern basis.

III.   SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
       The Group is principally engaged in toll road operation. The Group determines the specific accounting policies on the amortization of
       toll road operation rights according to the toll road industry characteristics. Refer to Note III 17 for details.

       1.      Statement of compliance

               The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the requirements of Accounting Standards for Business
               Enterprises or referred to as China Accounting Standards (“CAS”) issued by the MOF. These financial statements present
               truly and completely the consolidated financial position and financial position of the Company as at 31 December 2025, and
               the consolidated financial performance and financial performance and the consolidated cash flows and cash flows of the
               Company for the year then ended.

               These financial statements also comply with the disclosure requirements of “Regulation on the Preparation of Information
               Disclosures by Companies Issuing Securities, No. 15: General Requirements for Financial Reports” as revised by the China
               Securities Regulatory Commission (“CSRC”) in 2023. In addition, the financial statements were also subject to relevant
               disclosures required by the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance and the Listing Rules of the Stock Exchange.

       2.      Accounting period

               The accounting period is from 1 January to 31 December.

       3.      Operating cycle

               The Company takes the period from the acquisition of assets for processing to until the ultimate realisation of cash or
               cash equivalents as a normal operating cycle. Except for the real estate industry, the Group’s business cycle is short, and
               the determining criterion of asset-liability liquidity is 12 months. The real estate industry business cycle is from real estate
               development to sales realization, generally in more than 12 months, the specific period is determined according to the
               development conditions of the project, and its criterion of asset-liability liquidity is based on the business cycle.

       4.      Functional currency

               The Company’s functional currency is Renminbi, and these financial statements are presented in Renminbi. The functional
               currency is determined by the Company and its subsidiaries on the basis of the currency in which major income and costs
               are denominated and settled.

             6.     Accounting treatments for business combinations involving entities under common
                    control and not under common control
                    A transaction or event constitutes a business combination when the Group obtains control of one or more entities (or
                    a group of assets or net assets) which meet the definition of a business. Business combinations are classified as either
                    business combinations involving enterprises under common control or business combinations not involving enterprises
                    under common control.

                    For a transaction not involving enterprises under common control, the acquirer determines whether acquired set of assets
                    constitute a business. The Group may elect to apply the simplified assessment method, the concentration test, to determine
                    whether an acquired set of assets is not a business. If the concentration test is met and the set of assets is determined
                    not to be a business, no further assessment is needed. If the concentration test is not met, the Group shall perform the
                    assessment according to the guidance on the determination of a business.

                    When the set of assets the Group acquired does not constitute a business, acquisition costs should be allocated to each
                    identifiable assets and liabilities at their acquisition-date fair values. It is not required to apply the accounting of business
                    combination described as below.

                    (1)      Business combinations involving entities under common control

                             A business combination involving entities under common control is a business combination in which all of the
                             combining entities are ultimately controlled by the same party or parties both before and after the business
                             combination, and that control is not transitory. The assets acquired and liabilities assumed are measured based on
                             their carrying amounts in the consolidated financial statements of the ultimate controlling party at the combination
                             date. The difference between the carrying amount of the net assets acquired and the consideration paid for the
                             combination (or the total par value of shares issued) is adjusted against share premium in the capital reserve, with
                             any excess adjusted against retained earnings. Any costs directly attributable to the combination are recognised
                             in profit or loss when incurred. The combination date is the date on which one combining entity obtains control of
                             other combining entities.

                    (2)      Business combinations involving entities not under common control

                             A business combination involving entities not under common control is a business combination in which all of the
                             combining entities are not ultimately controlled by the same party or parties both before and after the business
                             combination. Where (1) the aggregate of the acquisition-date fair value of assets transferred (including the
                             acquirer’s previously held equity interest in the acquiree), liabilities incurred or assumed, and equity securities issued
                             by the acquirer, in exchange for control of the acquiree, exceeds (2) the acquirer’s interest in the acquisition-date
                             fair value of the acquiree’s identifiable net assets, the difference is recognised as goodwill. If (1) is less than (2), the
                             difference is recognised in profit or loss for the current period. The costs of issuing equity or debt securities as a
                             part of the consideration for the acquisition are included in the carrying amounts of these equity or debt securities
                             upon initial recognition. Other acquisition-related costs are expensed when incurred. Any difference between the
                             fair value and the carrying amount of the assets transferred as consideration is recognised in profit or loss. The
                             acquiree’s identifiable asset, liabilities and contingent liabilities, if the recognition criteria are met, are recognised by
                             the Group at their acquisition-date fair value. The acquisition date is the date on which the acquirer obtains control
                             of the acquiree.

III.   SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES (CONTINUED)
       7.   Criteria of control and preparation of consolidated financial statements

            (1)     General principles

                    The scope of consolidated financial statements is based on control and the consolidated financial statements
                    comprise the Company and its subsidiaries. Control exists when the investor has all of following: power over the
                    investee; exposure, or rights, to variable returns from its involvement with the investee and has the ability to affect
                    those returns through its power over the investee. When assessing whether the Group has power, only substantive
                    rights (held by the Group and other parties) are considered. The financial position, financial performance and cash
                    flows of subsidiaries are included in the consolidated financial statements from the date that control commences
                    until the date that control ceases.

                    When the accounting period or accounting policies of a subsidiary are different from those of the Company, the
                    Company makes necessary adjustments to the financial statements of the subsidiary based on the Company’s
                    own accounting period or accounting policies. Intra-group balances and transactions, and any unrealised profit or
                    loss arising from intra-group transactions, are eliminated when preparing the consolidated financial statements.
                    Unrealised losses resulting from intra-group transactions are eliminated in the same way as unrealised gains, unless
                    they represent impairment losses that are recognised in full in the financial statements.

            (2)     Subsidiaries acquired through a business combination

                    Where a subsidiary was acquired during the reporting period, through a business combination involving entities
                    under common control, the financial statements of the subsidiary are included in the consolidated financial
                    statements based on the carrying amounts of the assets and liabilities of the subsidiary in the financial statements
                    of the ultimate controlling party as if the combination had occurred at the date that the ultimate controlling party first
                    obtained control. The opening balances and the comparative figures of the consolidated financial statements are
                    also restated.

                    Where a subsidiary was acquired during the reporting period, through a business combination involving entities not
                    under common control, the identifiable assets and liabilities of the acquired subsidiaries are included in the scope
                    of consolidation from the date that control commences, based on the fair value of those identifiable assets and
                    liabilities at the acquisition date.

            (3)     Disposal of subsidiaries

                    When the Group loses control over a subsidiary, any resulting disposal gains or losses are recognised as investment
                    income for the current period.

            (4)     Changes in non-controlling interests

                    Where the Company acquires a non-controlling interest from a subsidiary’s non-controlling shareholders or
                    disposes of a portion of an interest in a subsidiary without a change in control, the difference between the
                    proportion interests of the subsidiary’s net assets being acquired or disposed and the amount of the consideration
                    paid or received is adjusted to the capital reserve (share premium) in the consolidated balance sheet, with any
                    excess adjusted to retained earnings.

       8.   Cash and cash equivalents

            Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash on hand, deposits that can be readily withdraw on demand, and short-term,
            highly liquid investments that are readily convertible into known amounts of cash and are subject to an insignificant risk of
            change in value.

      III.   SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES (CONTINUED)
             9.     Foreign currency transactions and translation of foreign currency financial statements

                    When the Group receives capital in foreign currencies from investors, the capital is translated to Renminbi at the spot
                    exchange rate at the date of the receipt. Other foreign currency transactions are, on initial recognition, translated to
                    Renminbi at the spot exchange rates on the dates of the transactions.

                    Monetary items denominated in foreign currencies are translated to Renminbi at the spot exchange rate at the balance
                    sheet date. The resulting exchange differences are generally recognised in profit or loss, except that differences related to a
                    specific-purpose borrowing denominated in foreign currency that qualify for capitalization are capitalized as part of the cost
                    of the qualifying asset during the capitalization period (see Note III.16). Non-monetary items that are measured at historical
                    cost in foreign currencies are translated to Renminbi using the exchange rate at the transaction date. Non-monetary items
                    that are measured at fair value in foreign currencies are translated using the exchange rate at the date the fair value is
                    determined. The resulting exchange differences are recognised in profit or loss, except for the differences arising from
                    the re-translation of equity investments at fair value through other comprehensive income, which are recognised in other
                    comprehensive income.

                    In translating the financial statements of a foreign operation, assets and liabilities of foreign operation are translated to
                    Renminbi at the spot exchange rate at the balance sheet date. Equity items, excluding retained earnings and the translation
                    differences in other comprehensive income, are translated to Renminbi at the spot exchange rates at the transaction dates.
                    Income and expenses of foreign operation are translated to Renminbi at the spot exchange rates at the transaction dates.
                    The resulting translation differences are recognised in other comprehensive income. The translation differences accumulated
                    in other comprehensive income with respect to a foreign operation are transferred to profit or loss in the period when the
                    foreign operation is disposed.

             10.    Financial instruments

                    Financial instruments include cash at bank and on hand, investments in equity securities other than those classified as
                    long-term equity investments (see Note III.12), receivables, payables, loans and borrowings, debentures payable and share
                    capital.

                    (1)     Recognition and initial measurement of financial assets and financial liabilities

                            A financial asset or financial liability is recognised in the balance sheet when the Group becomes a party to the
                            contractual provisions of a financial instrument.

                            A financial asset or financial liability is measured initially at fair value. For financial assets and financial liabilities at fair
                            value through profit or loss, any related directly attributable transaction costs are charged to profit or loss; for other
                            categories of financial assets and financial liabilities, any related directly attributable transaction costs are included
                            in their initial costs. A trade receivable, without significant financing component or practical expedient applied for
                            one year or less contracts, is initially measured at the transaction price in accordance with Note III.21.
